1: "Peteca" is a kind of ball with feathers used in various games. This expression relates to someone that never gives up and handles complicated situations.
2: Gaúcha(o) is someone who comes from the state of Rio Grande do Sul.
3: Mequetrefe is slang for someone or something that is not of the highest quality. It can be used in a funny or depreciative meaning.
4: Chimarrão is a hot drink prepared with "Mate" herbs, typically drank by Gaúchos.
5: In this context, we mean Brazilian funk, which is different from American funk.
6: "Jeitinho brasileiro" is a very broad concept related to Brazilian's ability to overcome obstacles. It can be in a good way, like mentioned in the video, but can also have a bad meaning, as if used for corruption.

L’any 2018 es va iniciar una campanya a Twitter amb l’objectiu de trobar les 10 paraules catalanes més boniques.
De totes les propostes que es van fer, es van seleccionar 25 mots per a la votació final.
En aquest vídeo us presentem les 10 paraules que van resultar guanyadores i us expliquem què signifiquen.
Per cert, aquesta campanya es va organitzar per celebrar el 150è aniversari de Pompeu Fabra, la persona que va establir la normativa de la llengua catalana. Sense ell, potser ara nosaltres no estaríem fent aquest vídeo.
Si voleu saber més coses sobre la figura de Pompeu Fabra i la seva obra, us en deixem alguns enllaços:
https://www.ccma.cat/tv3/alacarta/sen...
https://ca.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pompeu_...
https://www.upf.edu/web/portalpompeuf..."
---

Note: If the interviewees make mistakes, they will be corrected in the subtitles between brackets. If the interviewees say words in another language they will appear between square brackets. Furthermore, you’ll find the list of words that the interviewees have said and their corrections.

CU: Abbreviation for “Chinese University”(中大) or “CUHK”, which are abbreviations for “The Chinese University of Hong Kong” (香港中文大學).
CC: Abbreviation for “Chung Chi College” (崇基學院), one of the nine member colleges of the university.
五低/Ng Dai: Abbreviation for “Pentecostal Mission Hall Complex Low Block” (五旬節會樓低座). The word “五” (Ng) means “five” and is an abbreviation for “五旬節會樓” (Pentecostal Mission Hall Complex), while the word “低” (low) is an abbreviation for “低座” (Low Block).
應林/Ying Lin: Abbreviation for “Ying Lin Tang” (應林堂), a dormitory in Chung Chi College.
課金 (fo3 gam1): Originated from the Japanese word “課金” (kakin), originally means spending/being charged for something (esp. items in mobile games) in Japan, has become a common word in Hong Kong due to the popularity of Japanese mobile games.
UC: Abbreviation for “United College” (聯合書院), one of the nine member colleges of the university.
恒生/Hang Seng: Abbreviation for “Hang Seng Hall” (恒生樓), a dormitory in United College.
伯宿/Baak Suk: Abbreviation for “Bethlehem Hall” (伯利衡宿舍). The word “伯” (baak) is an abbreviation for “伯利衡” (Bethlehem), while the word “宿” (suk) is an abbreviation for “宿舍” (residential hall).
系莊/Hai Zong: Department societies, student organization that serves students of their own major/department. The word “系” is an abbreviation for “學系” (academic department), while “莊” (zong) is an abbreviation for “莊家”, which is a word often used in betting meaning “banker”.
sem: Abbreviation for “semester” (學期).
cred: Abbreviation for “credits” (學分).
reg: Abbreviation for “register”, which may also mean “apply for” (註冊、申請).
hall: Abbreviation for “residence hall”, or dormitory (宿舍).
FH: Abbreviation for “UGFH1001”, which is the course code for the course “In Dialogue with Humanity”. In this course, students study and discuss classic texts including but not limited to Plato’s “The Symposium”, “The Analects of Confucius”, The Bible, The Quran, and Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s “The Social Contract”. Ref: https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/oge_media/gef/doc/course_outlines/UGFH1001_readinglist.pdf
UG: Abbreviation for “University General Education” (大學通識), a series of compulsory courses for all CUHK students which cover a wide range of humanities, science and philosophical topics.
MTR: Abbreviation for “Mass Transit Railway”, the subway system in Hong Kong.

Avui ens porten les 5 millors pel·lícules en català. Primer, ens explicaran els actors i la trama. Llavors faran les votacions i al final veurem el rànquing.
Les pel·lícules que avui entren en acció són:
- Els dies que vindran: "Els dies que vindran" és un film de gènere romàntic i dramàtic en llengua catalana estrenat el 2019. És el tercer llargmetratge dirigit per Carlos Marqués-Marcet i està protagonitzat per David Verdaguer i Maria Rodríguez Soto.
- Estiu 1993: "Estiu 1993" és una comèdia dramàtica del 2017 dirigida per Carla Simón. La pel·lícula es va rodar a diverses poblacions de la Garrotxa l'estiu de 2016. Es tracta de la primera obra de la directora barcelonina, un "opera prima" que destaca pel gran nombre de nominacions i premis en festivals de cinema reconeguts internacionalment.
- Pa negre: "Pa negre" és una pel·lícula catalana escrita i dirigida pel mallorquí Agustí Villaronga i basada en la novel·la homònima d'Emili Teixidor. La pel·lícula barreja el gènere dramàtic, el misteri per saber la veritat dels crims i un toc fantàstic relacionat amb els somnis i fantasmes que s'ofereixen com a alternativa als ulls infantils del protagonista, qui marca el punt de vista de tot el relat.
- Salvador (Puig Antich): "Salvador (Puig Antich)" és un drama dirigit per Manuel Huerga, estrenat el setembre de 2006, basada en la novel·la "Compte enrere: la història de Salvador Puig Antich", escrita el 2001 pel periodista català Francesc Escribano.
- La vampira de Barcelona: "La vampira de Barcelona" és una pel·lícula catalana del 2020 dirigida per Lluís Danés. És un thriller històric basat en l'imaginari popular al voltant d'Enriqueta Martí, anomenada la «vampira del Raval» o «de Barcelona».
Escriviu-nos als comentaris quines són les millors pel·lícules en català i quina és la vostra classificació de les 5 millors pel·lícules en català.

Learn Dutch with street interviews: in this episode of Easy Dutch, Linus is asking people how they're celebrating King's Day in the Netherlands.
__
We recorded this video the day before King’s Day, which was on April 27. The reason for the celebration is the birthday of the Dutch King Willem-Alexander, however, as you might have seen in the video, for a lot of people it’s more about having fun and spending a nice day.  
Here a few explanations about the video: 
‘t – het 
Willem – short version of King Willem-Alexander  
Noorderplantsoen – urban public park in Groningen 
gezellig (adjective) – it could be translated as fun, social or cozy, depending on the context. We decided to not translate it, since it can not be translated perfectly. If you learn Dutch, this is really an essential word to learn. You will need it! A few examples: Hij/zij is gezellig (he/she is gezellig). Het was gezellig gisteren (it was gezellig yesterday). 

gezelligheid (noun) – Just like gezellig, it is also challenging to translate gezelligheid to English. Possible options would be ‘conviviality’, ‘sociability’ or ‘coziness’. 
Republican – We can only guess, but most likely the man was not referring to the political party in the USA, but to favoring and supporting a republic. 
Koningsmarkt – King’s market. We would recommend googling it and look at some pictures. Basically it is like a very big flea market.

* 6:10 - "Duits gedeelte" - Compared to the Netherlands, Belgium is a complicated country with a complex system of governance, 6 governments in total, structured on both regional and linguistic grounds. Belgium has a federal Belgian government and is divided into three highly autonomous regions, each with their own government too: Flanders in the north, Wallonia in the south, and the Brussels-Capital Region. Belgium is home to two main linguistic groups or communities: the Dutch-speaking Flemish Community (which has the same government as the Flemish regional government), about 60 percent of the population. Then there is the French-speaking Community, about 40 percent of the population. A small German-speaking Community, numbering around one percent, exists in the East Cantons. Both of these Communities have their own government too because the 3 regions of Belgium do not overlap with the languages spoken there, except for Flanders where the main language is Flemish. In Brussels however, the main language is French, followed by Flemish and a whole range of other international languages. The main language spoken in Wallonia is French and only a small part of it speaks German, close to the border with Germany. The three Communities represent the three official languages of Belgium: (Flemish) Dutch, French and German. This linguistic diversity also results in different and varied cultural identities which, culturally speaking, do not often interact with each other (different television channels, news outlets, etc.).  In comparison, the Netherlands is relatively straightforward with only one central government and both a linguistic and cultural unity as Dutch is the main and only standardized language with only some recognized provincial languages (mainly West Frisian) and regional dialects.

---
Remarks/Explanations on subtitles:

0:42 & 0:47 - O2 & A1 - It is a super common way to answer the question “What is your relationship status?” among the new generation in Hong Kong. The Alphabetical part refers to the current state of the person, A = alone /available, O = occupied, C = complicated. While the numerical part indicates how many times has the person been into romantic relationships. For example, O2 = occupied, currently in the second relationship; A1 = available, with one previous romantic relationship.

06:56 - 小孩子才做選擇 - This sentence literally means “Only the kids choose”. It has turned into a popular slang among Hong Kong and Taiwan in recent years. The sentence我全都要is quoted in Gau ban ji ma goon: Bak min Bau Ching Tin, which is a Hong Kong film with Stephen Chow in the cast. This sentence literally means “I want (them) all”. Anyway,「小孩子才做選擇，我全都要」has already become a popular slang in Hong Kong.

07:59 - 出到pool - 「出pool」is a common phrase describing the fact that you have found someone, or you are no longer single. That’s why you are “leaving the dating pool”.

08:33 & 09:58 - 加油 - “Add Oil” is a very iconic “Hong Kong English” expression to encourage someone. In 2018, “add oil” was made an official term in the Oxford English Dictionary.

08:38 & 09:35 - 食檸檬 - This phrase/slang literally means “eat lemon”. You are asking for something, but they just give you a lemon, especially the lemon is too sour, which means you are getting rejected.

---
* 4:11 - "Algemeen Nederlands" - This term means "Standard Dutch." Standard Dutch is used for public and official purposes, including instruction in schools and universities. Standard Dutch is quite uniform across Belgium and the Netherlands, though the accent, intonation and small vocabulary differences are indicative of where a speaker comes from.
Standard Dutch consists of two varieties: "Netherlandic Dutch" ("Nederlands-Nederlands", informally known in Flanders as "Hollands") as used in the Netherlands, and "Flemish Dutch" ("Vlaams-Nederlands" or "Belgisch-Nederlands") as used in Belgium. 
Bear in mind that when people talk about "Flemish", they either refer to the standardized variety of Flemish Dutch, or spoken informal Flemish, which consists of a great number of dialects, regionalects and "tussentaal." Tussentaal literally translates to "in between language", referring to its position between dialect and standardized Flemish Dutch.
The old name for Algemeen Nederlands is "Algemeen Beschaafd Nederlands", meaning "General Cultured Dutch". It's too complex to go into the history here, but it does say something about the elevated social status that was previously attributed to Standard Dutch. 
As a general indication, in this video you can hear various types of Flemish Dutch. Nout speaks Standard Flemish Dutch almost all of the times whereas most of the interviewees speak variations of Flemish, from dialect (like West Flemish) to tussentaal. As you can imagine, people that spoke dialect were harder to transcribe: in our transcriptions, we tried to find the middle ground between the language as spoken and legibility. This also meant that we sometimes had to sacrifice certain smaller exclamations or subject-verb links which you don't have in written language and which, if transcribed, would make the Dutch subtitles quite difficult to follow or understand. 

* 9:18 - poepen - This is a bit complicated but in tussentaal, it means "to have sex" whereas in standardized Netherlandic Dutch, it means "to poop".

What does the world need to know?
Is there something useful that everyone should know? 
What have you always wanted to share but nobody has ever asked you?
Do you have one piece of advice for the rest of the world?

Hola! Avui us explicarem com utilitzar el transport públic de Barcelona, com funcionen els bitllets pel metro, tren, ferrocarril, bus i tramvia i com comprar-los, així com també com pots llogar les bicicletes del Bicing. Aquestes són les preguntes que responem al vídeo:

- Perdona, em podries dir, on puc comprar un bitllet pel metro? - Excuse me, could you tell me where I can buy a metro ticket?
- Quin bitllet he de comprar? - Which ticket should I buy?
- Em pots ajudar a comprar un bitllet? - Can you help me buy a ticket?
- A on s'han de validar els bitllets? - Where do you validate the tickets?
- Puc fer transbord i utilitzar els diferents transports amb un mateix viatge? - Can I change and use different modes of transport in the same journey?
- Què són les zones? - What are the zones?
- Quanta estona falta perquè surti el següent? - How long until the next one is coming?
- Fins a quina hora funciona el metro? - What time does the metro run till? 
- Què passa si no valido el bitllet o viatjo sense? - What happens if I don't validate the ticket or I travel without?
- I si vull anar amb bicicleta? - And if I want to go by bike?
Enllaços d’interès:

Tarifes dels bitllets: https://www.tmb.cat/ca/tarifes-metro-bus-barcelona

Web de TMB: https://www.tmb.cat/ca/home
Alerta, per anar i tornar de l'aeroport necessites o bé el bitllet Aeroport o una “travel card”.
Compra els bitllets online: https://www.tmb.cat/ca/tarifes-metro-bus-barcelona/senzills-i-integrats/compra-bitllets-online

Si vols anar amb el telefèric de Montjuïc o el bus turístic hauràs de comprar bitllets diferents:
Telefèric de Montjuïc: https://www.telefericdemontjuic.cat/ca
Bus turístic: https://www.barcelonabusturistic.cat/ca
Mapa de zones: https://www.tmb.cat/ca/tarifes-metro-bus-barcelona/senzills-i-integrats/mapa-zones
Web de l’AMB: https://www.amb.cat/s/web/guest.html
Nitbus (servei nocturn d'autobusos): https://www.ambmobilitat.cat/principales/busquedanitbus.aspx
Lloguer de bicicletes:
L'aplicació Smou: https://www.smou.cat/
Bicing: https://www.bicing.barcelona/

Всем привет! 

Els vídeos que fem són per aprendre català i aquesta vegada hem volgut portar-vos les experiències dels alumnes que estudien la llengua catalana. 

The videos that we make are for learning Catalan and this time we wanted to bring you experiences from some students who are studying the Catalan language.

Aquest vídeo està centrat en Rússia i els estudiants de català russos. Esperem poder fer més vídeos com aquest, però en altres països del món, així que si apreneu català i voleu participar en els nostres vídeos, només ens heu d'escriure un missatge a qualsevol de les nostres xarxes socials o en els comentaris d'aquest vídeo. 

This video focuses on Russia and Russian students of Catalan. We hope to be able to make more videos like this in other countries around the world. So if you’re learning Catalan and you want to participate in our videos, you just have to send us a message on any of our social media or in the comments section for this video.

Volem agrair la col·laboració de totes les persones que han fet possible aquest vídeo. Moltes gràcies a tothom!

We want to thank the people who made this collaborative video possible. Thank you everyone!

Al vídeo hi veureu estudiants de català de Moscou i Sant Petersburg que aprenen català amb un professor particular, a la universitat (amb l'Institut Ramon Llull) o per lliure, amb materials en línia.

In the video you’ll see students of Catalan from Moscow and Saint Petersburg who are learning Catalan with a private teacher, at the university (with Institut Ramon Llull), or by themselves, with online materials.

Si vosaltres també apreneu català, escriviu-nos als comentaris com ho feu per aprendre la llengua, quins materials feu servir, quin so us costa més d'aprendre, quin és el vostre so preferit i si teniu cap anècdota divertida.

If you are also learning Catalan, write in the comments section how you’re learning the language, which materials you use, what you find the most difficult to learn, what is your favourite sound, and if you have a funny anecdote.

On Easy Catalan you’ll find videos in Catalan with subtitles in Catalan and English. The videos are made with Catalan learners and teachers in mind. 

En el vídeo d'aquest mes un proposem un joc! Heu de trobar les deu paraules que normalment escriuríem entre parèntesis.

In this month’s video we’re going to play a game! You have to find the ten words that we normally write in brackets. 

En el vídeo hi veieu una conversa telefònica entre l'Andreu i la Sílvia. A la Sílvia se li escapen 10 errors comuns en català. 

In the video, you’ll see a telephone conversation between Andreu and Sílvia. Sílvia lets slip 10 common Catalan errors.

Mireu-vos atentament el diàleg i intenteu endevinar les paraules que són calcs del castellà. No només heu d'intentar saber quines paraules són incorrectes, sinó també què s'hauria de dir.

Pay close attention to the dialogue and try to figure out the words that are borrowed from Spanish. Not only do you have to try and know which words are incorrect, but also what you should say.

Aquí teniu les solucions del joc:

Here are the answers to the game:

1.- *adelantar - avançar 
2.- *susto - esglai, espant, ensurt
3.- *anar-se - anar-se’n
4.- *casi - quasi, gairebé
5.- *ves amb cuidado / *ves al tanto - ves alerta / ves amb compte
6.- *en sèrio - de veritat, de veres, de debò, seriosament 
7.- *medir - mesurar, amidar, fer 
8.- *tamany - mida
9.- *a plaços - a terminis
10.- *vàries - alguns, diversos, diferents

1.- to overtake 
2.- fright
3.- to leave 
4.- almost
5.- be careful
6.- really, seriously 
7.- to measure
8.- size
9.- in instalments
10.- various, different

Els heu endevinat tots? Hi ha alguna paraula que feu servir normalment? Quina us ha sorprès més?

Did you figure them all out? Is there a word that you normally use? What surprised you the most?

Escriu-nos-ho en els comentaris!

Write to us in the comments.

Hem visitat Tarragona per parlar de 8 qüestions sobre el català:
We’ve visited Tarragona to find out 8 different things about Catalan:

A on es parla el català?
Quants parlants té el català?
El català és una llengua minoritària? Quina posició ocupa el català en nombre de parlants respecte a la resta de llengües de la Unió Europea?
El català s’estudia arreu del món?
De quin segle són els primers escrits que s’han trobat en català?
Quina posició ocupa la Viquipèdia en català respecte a la resta de llengües pel que fa al nombre d’articles?
És important, el català, en el món digital?
Què representa el domini .cat?

Where is Catalan spoken?
How many speakers of Catalan are there?
Is Catalan a minority language? How many speakers of Catalan are there compared to the other languages spoken in the European Union?
Is Catalan studied all over the world?

Ja sabies tot això sobre el català abans de veure el vídeo? Què has après? Escriu-nos-ho en els comentaris!

s, ss, c, ç
s, z

r, rr

ts, tz, tx, g, tj, dj
ny
x, sh

NOTE 1: Andreu speaks the Catalan from the Northwest whilst Sílvia speaks central Catalan. You’ll find that the most notable differences are in the pronunciation of the vowels. Easy Catalan makes videos in Catalan with subtitles in Catalan and English. The videos are made with Catalan learners and teachers in mind. In this video, we are in Girona. We want to show you around the city and everything you should know when going there.

En el vídeo preguntem:
Què em recomanaries fer a Girona?
I als voltants de Girona?
Quina és la teva activitat preferida dels caps de setmana?
A Girona hi ha molta tria de llocs on anar a menjar, on ens recomanaries anar? I què t'agrada menjar-hi?
Acaba la frase: Girona és...

In the video, we ask:
What would you recommend doing in Girona?
And on the outskirts of Girona?
What is your favourite thing to do on the weekends?
In Girona there are lots of places to go and eat, where would you recommend? And what do you like to eat there?

Finish the sentence: Girona is...
Has estat mai a Girona? La coneixes per alguna sèrie com Joc de Trons o pel·lícula? T'agradaria anar-hi? Escriu-nos-ho en els comentaris

Gràcies!

Have you ever been to Girona? Do you know it from a series like Game of Thrones or a film? Would you like to go? Answer this in the comments.

Thank you!

Easy Catalan crea material audiovisual en català per a aprenents i professors de català.  En aquest vídeo som a la Fira de Santa Llúcia, Barcelona, per explicar les tradicions nadalenques més curioses de Catalunya: el Tió i el Caganer. Dues tradicions força escatològiques, és a dir, que tenen a veure amb els excrements, o el que anomenem col·loquialment ‘caca’.
 
Easy Catalan creates audio visual content in Catalan for both Catalan learners and teachers. In this video we are at the Santa Llúcia Fair, in Barcelona, to explain the weridest Christmas traditions in Catalonia: the Tió and the Caganer. They are two quite scatological traditions, that’s to say that they have a lot to do with excrement, or as we say normally, ‘poo’.
 
1. Creus que els catalans som escatològics?
2. Com explicaries què és el tió a algú de fora?  
3. Què et caga normalment el tió?
4. Com celebreu aquesta tradició?
5. Saps d’on ve la tradició del tió?
6. Com explicaries què és el caganer a algú de fora?
7. Saps d’on ve la tradició del caganer?
8. Qui creus que es mereix el premi al caganer de l’any?
 
1. Do you think the Catalans are scatological?
2. How would you explain the Tió to a foreigner?
3. What does a Tió normally poop out for you?
4. How do you celebrate this tradition?
5. Do you know where the tradition of the Tió comes from?  
6. How would you explain what the Caganer is to a foreigner?
7. Do you know where the Caganer tradition comes from?
8. Who do you think deserves the Caganer of the Year award?  
 
Explica'ns tot això en els comentaris. A més a més, ens encantaria saber més tradicions curioses d'altres països. Si en saps, escriu-nos-les! :)
 
Esperem que aquest vídeo et serveixi, no només per veure que el català del carrer, sinó també per conèixer una mica més sobre la cultura catalana.
 
Write all of this in the comments section. Also, we would love to know more weird traditions from other countries. If you know any, tell us about them! :)
 
We hope that this video is useful, not only to see Catalan from the streets, but also to know a little bit more about Catalan culture.  
 
Nota: Si els entrevistats fan errors, els corregim en els subtítols entre parèntesis. Si els entrevistats diuen paraules en una altra llengua apareixeran entre claudàtors. A continuació trobeu la llista de paraules que han dit els entrevistats i la seva correcció.
 
Note: If the interviewees make mistakes, they will be corrected in the subtitles between brackets. If the interviewees say words in another language they will appear between square brackets. Furthermore, you’ll find the list of words that the interviewees have said and their corrections.

En el vídeo veieu les paraules comunes entre el català i l'espanyol, l'alemany, l'italià, el rus, l'àrab, el turc, el polonès, el francès, el danès, el romanès, l'anglès i el grec.


Easy Catalan creates audiovisual material in Catalan for learners and teachers of Catalan. In this video, we are in Cologne (Germany) with the other teams that make up Easy Languages. We recorded a video on words that we have in common between our languages. In the video you will see common words between Catalan and Spanish, German, Italian, Russian, Arabic, Turkish, Polish, French, Danish, Romanian, English and Greek.


Per tant, apareixen els integrants dels equips d'Easy Spanish, Easy German, Easy Italian, Easy Russian, Easy Arabic, Easy Polish, Easy French, Easy Danish, Easy Romanian, Easy English, Easy Greek i per suposat: Easy Catalan.

There are many common words that exist in Catalan and other languages, but in the this video we couldn’t mention them all, so if you think of any more, write them to us in the comments section.


Si saps altres llengües que no apareixen al vídeo, però també tenen paraules en comú amb el català, també ens les escrius :)

If you know other languages that don’t make an appearance in the video, but also have words in common with Catalan, also get in touch :)


Esperem que aquest vídeo et serveixi, no només per veure que el català té moltes paraules comunes amb altres llengües, sinò també com a llista de vocabulari nou.

1 - Azizliğine uğramak (Being exposed to something’s/someone’s sainthood): This idiom is used when someone is tricked or harmed by something or someone.
2 - Bey/Hanım: Bey is a Turkish honorific, very much like the English honorifics (Mr., Mrs. or Ms.) but we use it AFTER the first name, not before the last name. Bey is used for males, and Hanım is used for females.

Easy Catalan makes videos in Catalan for everyone who wants to learn the language. In this video we’re in Barcelona. It is the 11th September 2019, the National Day of Catalonia. For many years people take part in a protest to celebrate this day and we will ask the people why they want Catalan independence.

The National Day of Catalonia, 11th September, commemorates the defeat that the Catalans suffered in 1714.

Preguntes i respostes que podem aprendre en el vídeo:

Ets en una cafeteria, com demanaries un cafè?
Un cafè, si us plau.
Em podria servir un cafè amb llet, si us plau?
Jo voldria un tallat, si us plau.
Jo vull un cafè americà.
Em podria portar un cafè descafeïnat, si us plau?
Per mi un cigaló, si us plau.
A mi posa’m un cafè, també.
Jo volia un cafè sol.

You’re in a café, how would you order a coffee?
One coffee, please.
Could I have a flat white, please?
I would like an espresso with a little milk, please.
I would like an americano.
Could I get a decaf coffee, please?
I’d like an espresso with a dash of alcohol, please.
I’ll also get a coffee.
I would like an espresso.

Sol o amb llet? Si vols llet: sencera, condensada, desnatada, de soja, d’arròs...?
Amb sucre, sacarina o sense sucre?
Si vols un cigaló: De què el vols? Conyac, whisky, rom, anís...
Si vols un cafè descafeïnat: de sobre o de màquina?

With or without milk? If you want it with milk, would you rather it full fat, condensed, skimmed, soya, rice…?
Do you want any sugar or sweetener?
What alcohol do you want with your espresso? Cognac, whisky, rum, anise…?

GLOSSARY:
1 – Şekil A (Figure A): In school textbooks and other certain documents, it is common to see remarks such as “As seen in Figure A”. This remark has become a popular slang in Turkish spoken language, often used to bring attention to something we want to show or demonstrate.
 
2 – Şefim (My Chef): In Turkish, we use the possessive suffix when we address people in certain professions. These include: Teachers (Hocam or Öğretmenim), Chefs (Şefim), Police officers (Komiserim) and military commanders (Komutanım). Note that this is NOT the case for all professions.
 
3 – Tüketmek (Consume): In Turkish, this is a slightly more formal way of saying “eat”, similar to “Consume” in English, although it is more commonly used in daily speech than in English.

Saber dir les hores en català:
Telling the time in Catalan:

Per dir les hores exactes és diu directament el número de l'u al dotze, de vegades implica haver d'explicitar la part del dia a què correspon una hora determinada: del migdia, de la tarda, del vespre, etc.:
12:00 Les dotze (en punt)
19:00 Són les set (de la tarda)

To say the exact ‘on the hour’ time, you say a number from one to twelve. Sometimes you have to specify what time of day you mean: midday, in the afternoon, in the evening, etc:
12:00 twelve o’clock (exactly)
19:00 seven o’clock (in the afternoon)

Per dir quan és “i quinze” direm: “un quart” i l'hora que vindrà:
16:15 un quart de cinc

To say ‘quarter past’ we say: ‘un quart’ and that hour that approachs:
16:15 quarter past five

Quan és “i trenta” direm: “dos quarts” i l'hora que vindrà:
16.30 dos quarts de cinc

When it’s ‘half past’ we say: ‘dos quarts’ and the hour that approaches:
16:30 half past five

Quan és “i quaranta-cinc” direm: “tres quarts” i l'hora que vindrà:
16.45 tres quarts de cinc

When it’s ‘quarter to’ we say: ‘tres quarts’ and the hour that approaches:
16.45 quarter to five

També podem escoltar les expressions: "les quatre i quart", "les quatre i mitja" i “les quatre i tres quarts”.

We also hear expressions such as ‘four fifteen’, ‘half four’ and ‘four forty-five’.

To tell the times in between the quarter hours, we say the hour and the minutes. For example:
13:05 five past one
14:10 ten past two
18:25 twenty-five past six
21:56 four minutes to ten

Una altra forma d'expressar és utilitzant els verbs: “passar” i “faltar”
13:05 Passen cinc minuts de la una.
14:10 Passen deu minuts de les dues.
18:25 Falten cinc minuts per a dos quarts de set.
21:56 Falten quatre minuts per a les deu.

Another way of telling the time is to use the verbs ‘passar’ and ‘faltar’
13:05 it’s five past one.
14:05 it’s ten past two.
18:25 it’s twenty-five past six.
21:56 it’s four minutes to ten.

Les informacions en què cal molta precisió horària, diem les hores de la una fins a les vint-i-tres:
L'autobús de les 7.23 (set vint-i-tres) no ha passat fins a les 10.48 (deu quaranta-vuit)
El tren de les 16.27 (setze vint-i-set) encara no ha passat.
Aquest vespre, a les 21.54 (vint-i-una cinquanta-quatre) programació especial.

For information that requires more precision, we use the twenty-four hour clock:
The 7:23 (seven twenty-three) bus did not arrive until 10:48 (ten fourty-eight)
The 16:27 train (sixteen twenty-seven) still has not arrived.
This evening, at 21:54 (twenty-one fifty-four) there is a TV special.


Altres expressions per a precisar uns minuts abans o després dels quarts són:
05.14 vora un quart de sis
05.29 gairebé dos quarts de sis
05.47 tres quarts tocats de sis
06.02 les sis tocades
14.05 les dues ben tocades
de 02.05 a 02.10 mig quart de tres
de 05.35 a 05.40 dos quarts i mig de sis
de 02.20 a 02.40 va arribar a quarts de tres

Other ways to tell the time before and after the quarter hour are:
05:14 just before quarter past five
05:29 almost five thirty
05:47 just after quarter to six
06:02 just after six
14:05 just after two
From 02:05 to 2:10 almost quarter past three
From 05:35 to 05:40 almost quarter to six
From 02:20 to 02:40 it was almost quarter to three

Write some time phrases or explain a normal day in the comments. If you still aren’t sure about how to tell the time, you can ask below the video. Thanks for looking at our videos :)

Note: If the interviewees make mistakes, they will be corrected in the subtitles within brackets.

---
1 - Gonya: “Konya” in Konya Accent.

2 - I would die (Ölürüm): In this context, this phrase expresses affection, i.e. the person saying it would be willing to die for his country.

3 - My Turkey (Türkiyem): Sometimes, in Turkish, using a possessive suffix expresses affection, not possession.

4 - Inshallah (İnşallah): An statement of arabic origin, mainly used by muslims. It literally translates to “God willing” or “If God wills”.

5 - Super (Süper): Same as the English “Super”. It is commonly and informally used in positive exclamations.

6 - The suffixes in these sentences might seem a little off because of the local accent. The proper words are "gidersin" and "yaparsın"; "giden" and "yapan" are vocally shortened versions in the Konyan accent. These can be easily confused with the actual words "giden" or "yapan" in proper Turkish, which mean "people who go" and "people who do" respectively.

7 - A verse from the Adhan, the Islamic Call to Prayer. This particular verse roughly means “Rush to Prayer”.

8 - Hodja (Hoca, Hocam): This word means Master or Teacher in Turkish, originating from the Ottoman Period. It is mainly used for Islamic scholars and imams who have considerable knowledge of the Quran and theology, like in this instance. Today, the use of this word extends to formal school teachers and even certified experts on any particular topic.

9 - Let me tell my mister (Efendime Söyleyeyim): This phrase has no definite meaning, and is mainly used as a vocalized pause in Turkish.

Ramadan (Ramazan) – Ninth month of the lunar Islamic calendar, in which the Quran was revealed to Prophet Muhammad. It is considered a holy month, during which muslims fast from early morning (Suhur) until the evening (Iftar) in order to emphatize with starving and needy people.

Eid ul-Fitr (Ramazan Bayramı) – A three-day religious holiday at the end of Ramadan.

Blessing (Nimet) – Muslims consider all food (with the exception of forbidden food like pork meat) a blessing from Allah. When talking about food in religious contexts, it is common to use the word Nimet, the word for blessing in Turkish.

Namaz/Five Daily Prayers – Namaz is one of the five pillars of Islam, a kind of worship which is the duty of all Muslims to perform five certain times a day. It can either be performed in private, or in mosques with others.

Suhur (Sahur) – Every day during Ramadan, muslims wake up early in the morning, before the dawn, to have a meal before the fasting period begins, in order to prepare themselves for a day without any food or drink. This time is called Suhur (or Sahur in Turkish).

Adhan/Call to Prayer (Ezan) – A call to worship recited five times a day from the mosque minarets. It informs all muslims that the time for prayer has come, and summons them to perform the Namaz.

Sıla-i Rahim – An islamic tradition which dictates that muslims should keep in touch with their relatives and friends; they should visit them and communicate with them, forgive resentments against them and have mutual love and respect.

Aquí sota teniu els números en català:
Just below you have the numbers in Catalan:

Del zero al dinou:
From zero to nineteen:

0 – zero

3 – tres

Excepció:
Exceptions:

The hundreds:

D-U-C:
Es posa guionet entre les desenes i les unitats (per exemple cinquanta-quatre) i entre les unitats i les centenes (per exemple dos-cents).
T-U-H (Tens-(single)Unit-Hundred)
A dash is placed between the tens and the single units (for exemple fifty-five) and between the single units and the hundreds (e.g. two hundred).

*:  ‘Baba (Pops)’ is not meant to address a senior in this context; it is one of the many slangs Turkish youth use to address each other.
*: 'Hacı ( Hadji)is normally used to address Muslims who have completed their Hajj pilgrimage, but like ‘ Baba (Pops)’, sometimes this word is also used as a slang by the Turkish youth to address each other.
*:  ‘Hayırlı olsun (May it be fortunate)’ is a phrase in Turkish often used to congratulate someone. When something good has happened to someone, we use this phrase to wish everything goes well for them.
*:  ‘Kolay gelsin (May it be easy) is a phrase in Turkish often used to wish someone’s work gets more easy for them.
*:  Abi (Big brother) or Abla (Big sister) is a common way to address unrelated seniors in Turkish.
*:  ‘Damlaya damlaya göl olur’ word for word: ‘Dripping drops make a lake.’ Actual meaning:  This proverb means a small amount of something (such as money) can accumulate to a great amount if we are patient. Sometimes, it also means that we can achieve great things with small steps.
*: ‘Dam üstünde saksağan, vur beline kazmayı.’ word for word: ‘Magpie on the roof, tie the pickaxe on your waist’. Actual meaning: This  proverb is used in Turkish as a response to something unrelated to the topic or something that doesn’t make sense.
*: 'Ayağını yorganına göre uzat.' word for word: ‘Stretch your feet according to your quilt’. Actual meaning: This proverb means one should consider his/her finances when making spendings.
*: 'Sakla samanı, gelir zamanı.' word for word: 'Hide the hay, time may come for it'. Actual meaning: It has the same meaning as 'Keep a thing for seven years and you'll always find a use for it.'
*: 'Bal dök yala.' word for word: 'Pour honey on it and lick it'. Actual meaning: We say this to point out something that is very clean and tidy.
*: 'Keser döner sap döner, gün gelir hesap döner.': word for word: 'Hatchet turns, handle turns, one day the score turns'. Actual meaning: This proverb means things can always take an unexpected turn, and our affairs might not always go as we planned.
*: 'Çam devirmek': word for word: 'Toppling the pine tree': Actual meaning: We say ‘he/she toppled the pine tree’ when someone commits a faux pas (an embarrassing blunder) during conversations.
*: 'Saman altından su yürütmek' word for word: 'Running water under the hay' Actual meaning: We say someone ‘runs water under the hay’ when he/she does something without anyone noticing, usually with the intent of making trouble.

1) verd: (0:15-0:28)
verd (masculí singular), verda (femení singular), verds (masculí plural), verdes (femení plural)
1) green (verd): (0:15-0:28)
verd (masculine singular), verda (femenine singular), verds (masculine plural), verdes (femenine plural)

blanc (m.sing.), blanca (f. sing.), blancs (m. pl.), blanques (f. pl.)
2) white (blanc): (0:33-0:49)
blanc (m.sing.), blanca (f. sing.), blancs (m. pl.), blanques (f. pl.)

3) negre: (0:52-1:12)
Alerta! El masculí singular és acabat amb –e (negre), el femení singular amb –a (negra) i el plural és negres.

Careful! Masculine singular ends with –e (negre), the feminine singular ends with –a (negre) and the plural is negres.

groc (m.sing.), groga (f. sing.), grocs (m. pl.), grogues (f. pl.)
4) yellow (groc): (1:16-1:126)
groc (m.sing.), groga (f. sing.), grocs (m. pl.), grogues (f. pl.)

Per al singular marró i per al plural marrons.

For the singular it’s marró and for the plural it’s marrons.

gris (m.sing.), grisa (f. sing.), grisos (m. pl.), grises (f. pl.)
6) grey (gris): (1:40-1:54)
gris (m.sing.), grisa (f. sing.), grisos (m. pl.), grises (f. pl.)

blau (m.sing.), blava (f. sing.), blaus (m. pl.), blaves (f. pl.)
7) blue (blau): (1:55-2:06)
blau (m.sing.), blava (f. sing.), blaus (m. pl.), blaves (f. pl.)

- Soc ...

0:36

- Visc a...

- I live in...

0:44

Which languages do you speak?
- I speak...

On has viscut?

- I’ve lived in...

Learn Catalan with Easy Catalan! In our first Super Easy we explain greetings and farewells. Do you know how to say hello when you meet someone in the street?
Note: If the interviewees make errors, we will correct them in the subtitles using parenthesis.

Salutacions:
Greetings:
Hola / Hello - 00:10
Bon dia / Good morning [also used throughout the day] - 00:19
Bon dia i bona hora / [a longer and less common variant for 'Bon dia', but with the same meaning] - 00:26
Bona tarda / Good afternoon - 00:32
Bones, Ep, Ei / Hey! - 00:37
Déu vos guard / God bless you [literally, 'May God watch over you'] - 00:45


Comiats:
Farewells:
Adeu / Bye - 01:23
Adeu-siau / Goodbye - 01:33
Fins aviat, fins demà, fins després, fins dimarts, fins més tard... /
See you soon, see you tomorrow, see you later, see you Tuesday, see you later... - 01:39
Bona nit / Goodnight/night - 01:51
Salut, que vagi bé, passiu-ho bé, arreveure /
See you, all the best, have fun/enjoy, see you - 02:05

Learn Catalan with Easy Catalan - Today we are in Barcelona, in 36a edició de la Setmana del Llibre en català/36th annual Catalan book week and we ask the people about which kind of books did they read and the best books for beginners.
Note: If the interviewees make mistakes, the subtitles will be corrected in brackets.

Aprèn català amb Easy Catalan! Avui som a Barcelona, a la 36a edició de la Setmana del Llibre en català. Preguntem a la gent quins llibres han llegit i quin llibre recomanarien per a aprenents del català.
Nota: Si els entrevistats fan errors, seran corregits en els subtítols entre parèntesis.

Here are the recommended books for Catalan learners:

Aquí teniu els llibres recomanats per a aprenents de català:
- Col·lecció sobre els llibres d'en Teo: https://www.grup62.cat/index.php?tipo=colecciones&nombre=teo&col=G620000635&q=15&pag=1
- Revista Cavall Fort: http://cavallfort.cat/
- El perquè de tot plegat (Quim Monzó): http://www.quadernscrema.com/cataleg/el-perque-de-tot-plegat/
- Ronda naval sota la boira (Pere Calders): http://www.magrana.cat/ronda-naval-sota-la-boira_pere-calders_libro-OMAC087-ct.html
- La plaça del diamant (Mercè Rodoreda): https://www.grup62.cat/llibre-la-placa-del-diamant/100478
- El triomf de la imaginació. 60 invents que han canviat el món (o gairebé) (Ròmul Brotons): https://albertieditor.cat/index.php?route=product/product&path=89&product_id=57

And here are the books that were bought or read:

I aquí els llibres que han comprat o llegit:
- El Clan de Sa Ràpita (Montserrat Espallargas): https://www.pageseditors.cat/ca/el-clan-de-sa-rapita.html
- El nom del vent (Patrick Rothfuss): http://elbiblionauta.com/ca/2015/01/25/el-nom-del-vent-2007-patrick-rothfuss/
- El cor de les tenebres (Joseph Conrad): https://www.grup62.cat/llibre-el-cor-de-les-tenebres/94374
- El teatre d'en Sabbath (Philip Roth): http://www.magrana.cat/el-teatre-den-sabbath_philip-roth_libro-OMAC394-ct.html
- Aquell antic missatge de l'amor (Vicenç Llorca): https://www.grup62.cat/llibre-aquell-antic-missatge-de-lamor/273215
- El bibliobús de la llibertat (Miquel Joseph): http://simboleditors.com/home/28-el-bibliobus-de-la-llibertat-9788495987617.html
- Walden o la vida als boscos (Henry David Thoreau): http://simboleditors.com/130-walden-9788415315018.html
- Dones de Barcelona (Elisenda Albertí): https://albertieditor.cat/index.php?route=product/product&product_id=61
- Dames, reines, abadesses (Elisenda Albertí): https://albertieditor.cat/index.php?route=product/product&keyword=Cartes%2520i%2520carters.%2520Una%2520hist%25C3%25B2ria%2520del%2520correu%2520postal%2520a%2520Barcelona&product_id=56
- (En espanyol/Spanish) No es medianoche quien quiere (Antonio Lobo Antunes): https://www.megustaleer.com/libros/no-es-medianoche-quien-quiere/MES-073192
- Populisme. El llenguatge de l'adulació de les masses (Ferran Sáez Mateu): http://www.pamsa.cat/pamsa/cataleg/Populisme-El-llenguatge-de-ladulacio-de-les-mases.html
- (En espanyol/Spanish) Al faro (Virginia Woolf): https://www.edhasa.es/libros/114/al-faro
- (En espanyol/Spanish) Insurgente (Veronica Roth): http://www.editorialmolino.com/insurgente_veronica-roth_libro-MONL088-ct.html
- L'ofici d'historiador (Josep Fontana): https://www.arcadia-editorial.com/llibres/lofici-dhistoriador/
- Entre dos mons: El dibbuq (S.An-Ski): http://editorialmalesherbes.com/cataleg.php

Esperem que llegiu molt!

We hope you get to read a lot!

---
In this episode Lucas and I will sing for you so that you can see how great it is to learn Portuguese with music. Not only do we have great music in Brazil, but also great people, who always help us. So, herewith we thank our new volunteer Wesley very much for his input. In the video we are talking about the Pretérito Perfeito Simples which is not 100% the same thing as the simple past, neither is it the present perfect. Every language has their own rules and that is why in our translation the Portuguese Pretérito Perfeito Simples sometimes corresponds to the use of the simple past and sometimes to the present perfect in the English Language. 

So, let us know in the comments, if you know some songs that would fit into this topic of using the regular past in Portuguese?

Thank you all very much for your support!

Un mystère

Il appelle Antoine et Sandrine. D'habitude, à l'heure où ils s'en vont, la mystérieuse villa bleue dort encore. Aujourd'hui, par la grille ouverte, il aperçoivent portes cassées et vitres brisées. ENGLISH TRANSLATION (by the way, I think I will do either translation, either but some translated words, what do you think?)

A mystery

This morning, as every day since the beginning of the summer, the children are getting dressed, are getting ready and leave to the beach with their monitors. Suddenly, on the way, David stops all of a sudden. He calls Antoine and Sandrine. Usually, at the moment of the departure, the mysterious blue villa is still sleeping. Today, through the open metal gate, they are glimpsing fractured doors and broken windows. What is happening?

HERE is the NEW dictation, it's a bit fast and I advise you to PAUSE the dictation when you need a bit more time. Otherwise, it's quite SIMPLE and suitable for BEGINNERS. You can find the TEXT and a very complete VOCABULARY underneath:

TEXT:
Une porte s'ouvre au milieu de nulle part. Je vois enfin quelqu'un, un visage souriant qui me regarde. Je ne suis pas habitué à vivre ce genre d'expériences mais je demande : « Qui êtes-vous ?» Aucune réponse. J'ai l'impression d'être dans un film, ceux dans lesquels des personnes sont choisies pour vivre des aventures merveilleuses. Je ne savais pas qu'il pouvait se passer de choses aussi étranges dans la vraie vie. Quelqu'un m'attrape par le bras, fermement, je ne veux pas. Soudain, je regarde au mur. Il y a quelque chose de tout à fait anormal, je comprends, j'attrape mon agresseur et je le fais voler à travers la maison. Il est temps de voir où tout cela va me mener.

VOCABULARY:
Une porte s'ouvre = A door opens
Nulle part = nowhere
Enfin = eventually
Un visage = a face
Je suis habitué = I'm used to
Genre d'expériences = kind a experiences
Qui êtes-vous? = Who are you?
aucune réponse = no answer
ceux dans lesquels = those in which
Je savais = I knew
Se passer = to take place
Etrange = strange
Dans la vraie vie = in real life
Quelqu'un m'attrape par le bras = someone grabs me by the arm
Soudain = all of a sudden
Je regarde au mur = I'm looking at (what's on) the wall
Anormal = abnormal
tout à fait = completely
J'attrape = I grab (but this verb mainly means "to catch")
agresseur = attacker
Je le fais voler voler à travers la maison = I throw him through the house (this is an informal French expression, "voler" means "to fly" and also "to steal" but not in this context).
Il est temps = It's time
où tout cela va nous mener = where all that is going to lead us

Text:
Le jour se lève. J'ouvre un œil, puis l'autre. Je regarde autour de moi, il n'y a pas beaucoup de lumière. Où suis-je? Je me réveille dans un endroit que je ne connais pas. J'ai un peu peur. Quoi qu'il en soit, je vais devoir explorer ce lieu. Je sors du lit, je m'habille avec ce que je trouve et je marche vers la porte. Je quitte la petite pièce sans savoir ce que je vais trouver de l'autre côté. Il y a beaucoup de lumière de l'autre côté, beaucoup plus que de là où je viens. Content de quitter ce lieu que je ne connais pas, je pars m'aventurer dans cette maison que je n'ai jamais vue.

Le jour se lève = Morning comes
Un endroit/lieu = a place
Connaître = to know
Beaucoup de lumière = a lot of light
ce que je trouve = what I find
Je sors du lit = I go out of bed
Je m'habille = I get dressed
quitter = to leave
de l'autre côté = on the other side

title: Vila Autódromo // The Story of a Community | Easy Brazilian Portuguese 24
description:
Learn Portuguese with Brazilian Portuguese! Thank you all for coming back to watch this new episode. The Vila Autódromo was a big community, located in Jacarepagua, near Barra da Tijuca in rio de Janeiro. The community (you don't call them Favelas anymore out of respect) was destroyed because it occupied some space that was needed for the construction of the Olympic Village. The removal was violent and full of conflicts. A small part of the community fought until the utmost and managed to stay on the territory. The prefecture built social housings for them to live in. Dona Maria is an important spokesperson of the community and we had the honour to meet her and hear her story.

description:

Notes on this episode:

1) “Dar uma palinha”
Diminutive form of “dar uma pala”. A sample, a taster, a sneak preview of upcoming content.
 
2) Gringo
Masculine noun
Inf. Foreigner, tourist. Unlike in Hispanic culture where this could be perceived as a pejorative name for Americans, in Brazil “gringo” encompasses any person of foreign nationality and has no negative connotations at all.

3) “Vem de berço”
Phrase meaning “it’s in his/her genes”, “they were born to do it”

4) “Voar”
“To fly” can have a similar meaning in English: to succeed, to excel at something.

title: Places ending with -ria | Easy Brazilian Portuguese 14
description:
Learn Portuguese with Easy Brazilian Portuguese! In this episode Kristina is asking people about places ending with -ria!
 
As stated before, spoken Portuguese differs a lot from grammatically correct language rules. A good example is the desperation of teachers who explain to their foreign students over and over again, that they should use the preposition "a" (to) with the verb "ir" (go) but once they walk out of the classroom all they actually hear and say is "ir em" (go in). This is why we said in the video: "Você já foi em uma?" instead of "Você já foi a uma?". So, you write "ir a" and you can say "ir em". Don't worry too much! Language is alive and underlying changes and adaption throughout its history!

Justyna is asking Poles what they like about Germany and Cari is asking Germans what they like about Poles. The two videos were filmed and edited during the Polish-German Media Camp in Katowice, which brought together 20 young people from Poland and Germany to work together on video projects about the relations and connections between the two countries. Today, you can find a translation of the first dictation : rencontre avec la fleur. It will help you understand better the meaning of this dictation.

Le petit prince traversa le désert 
The little prince crossed the desert 

et ne rencontra qu'une fleur. 
and met with only one flower. 

Une fleur à trois pétales, 
It was a flower with three petals, 

une fleur de rien du tout... 
a flower of no account at all... 

- Bonjour, dit le prince. 
- Good morning, said the prince. 

- Bonjour, dit la fleur. 
- Good morning, said the flower. 

- Où sont les hommes? 
- Where are the men? 

demanda poliment le petit prince. 
the little prince asked, politely. 

La fleur, un jour, avait vu passer une caravane : 
The flower had once seen a caravan passing. 

- Les hommes ? Il en existe, je crois, six ou sept. 
- Men ? she echoed. I think there are six or seven of them in existence. 

Je les ai aperçus il y a des années. 
I saw them, several years ago. 

Mais on ne sait jamais où les trouver. 
But one never knows where to find them. 

Le vent les promène. 
The wind blows them away. 

Ils manquent de racines, ça les gêne beaucoup. 
They have no roots, and that makes their life very difficult. 

-Adieu, fit le petit prince. 
"Goodbye," said the little prince. 

-Adieu, dit la fleur. 
"Goodbye," said the flower.’

Here's the transcript to help you learn quicker :

Avoir
To have

Avoir est un synonyme de posséder.
Having is a synonymous of possessing.

Je veux avoir ça!
I want to have it!

J'ai de la chance.
I'm lucky.

Je n'ai pas compris.
I haven't understood.

Est-ce que j'ai faim? Oui!
Am I hungry? Yes, I am!

Tu as beaucoup de plantes chez toi.
You've got a lot of plants at your place.

Est-ce que tu as soif?
Are you thursty?

Il a des choses à dire.
He has things to say.

On n'a plus envie de venir ici.
We don't wish to come here anymore.

Avons-nous le temps?
Do we have time?

Vous n'avez pas l'air très contents.
You don't look very happy.

Elles n'ont pas d'argent pour payer l'amende.
They don't have money to pay the fine.

Est-ce que tu as eu ce que tu voulais?
Did you get what you wanted?

Nous avons eu chaud.
That was a close one for us.

Ils n'ont eu que ce qu'ils méritaient.
They've only got what they deserved.

On avait envie d'aller jusqu'au bout.
We wanted to go up until the end.

Elle avait deux gros chiens.
She had two big dogs.

Nous avions dix ans cet été là.
We were ten years old that summer.

J'aurais de l'énergie si je ne me couchais pas si tard.
I would be energetic if I would't go to sleep that late.

T'aurais pas dix euros à me dépanner?
Would you have ten euros to help me out?

Tais-toi! Nous n'aurions pas eu de problèmes 
Shut up! We wouldn't have got into trouble

si nous ne t'avions pas écouté.
if we ever not listened to you.

J'aurai toujours un moment pour t'écouter.
I will always find a moment to listen to you.

Tu auras tout ce que tu veux.
You will have all that you like.

Vous aurez beau crier, on ne vous écoutera pas plus.
However much you shout, we won't listen to you more than that.

Il faut avoir 18 ans pour pouvoir entrer ici.
You must be 18 to enter here.

Pour prendre l'avion, il faut que j'aie mon passeport.
In order to fly, I need to have my passport.

J'aimerais qu'elle ait plus de temps à m'accorder.
I'd like her to spend more time with me.

Est-ce que t'aimerais pas avoir un nouveau téléphone?
Wouldn't you like to have a new phone?

On aimerait qu'il arrête de chanter.
We'd like him to stop singing.

Ayez confiance!
Have trust!

Mes amis, n'ayons pas peur!
My friends, let's not fear!

Aie de la patience avec ton chat.
Be patient with you cat.

INTRODUCTION TO THE NEW SERIES

Bonjour à tous et bienvenue sur Easy French!
Hi everyone and welcome to Easy French!

En ce moment, j'apprends l'allemand.
I'm learning German at the moment.

J'apprends l'Allemand, ce n'est pas évident
I'm learning German, it's not so easy

et de quoi est-ce que j'ai le plus besoin
and what do I need most

pour comprendre cette langue?
to understand this language?

La réponse, c'est : les verbes!
The answer is: verbs!

J'ai besoin de verbes parce que les verbes sont,
I need verbs because verbs are,

en quelque sorte, l'essence de l'action.
in a way, the essence of action.

Les verbes permettent de tout expliquer.
Verbs allow to explain everything.

Même si vous ne connaîssez pas tous les mots
Even if you don't know all the words

de la phrase, si vous connaîssez une ciquantaine
in the sentence, if you know about fifty

ou une centaine de verbes, vous ne serez pas perdus.
or about a hundred verbs, you won't be lost.

Donc, j'ai décidé de créer cette série de vidéos
So, I decided to create this video series

afin de vous aider à apprendre ces verbes essentiels
in order to help you lean these essential verbs

et, à savoir aussi, quels sont les temps
and, including also the most

les plus importants en français. Je ne dis pas
important tenses in French. I don't say

qu'il y a des temps réellement moins importants.
that some tenses really are less important.

Mais pour l'usage, dans la vie quotidienne,
But as for when you use it, in daily life,

vous n'aurez besoin, peut-être, que de six ou sept temps.
you might perhaps only need six or seven tenses.

Donc, on va utiliser ces temps-là en particulier
So, we're going to use these particular tenses

et ça va, je l'espère, vous aider.
and this, I hope, will help you.

Donc, donnez-nous vos retours sur ces vidéos-là,
So, give us feedbacks on those videos,

la première et la deuxième vidéo seront un peu cut.
the first and second video will flow a bit fast.

Donc, ne vous inquiétez pas, ce ne seront que les deux
So, don't worry, these will only be the two

premières parce que je faisais des essais et que j'ai fait
first videos because I was doing some tests and I made

quelques petites erreurs.
several small mistakes.

Donc, je vous dit : à plus tard ou même
So then: see you later or even

à tout de suite pour la vidéo. Salut!
right now for the video. Bye!

BEGINNING OF THE EPISODE

Être ou ne pas être, telle est la question.
To be or not to be, that is the question.

Comment peut-on faire pour être heureux?
How can we to do it to be happy?

Je suis fatigué.
I'm tired.

Je ne suis pas très grand.
I'm not very tall.

Suis-je au bon endroit?
Am I at the right place?

Tu es mon ami.
You are my friend.

Est-ce que tu es chez toi?
Are you at home?

Il est vraiment intelligent!
He's so smart!

On est ici pour voir le concert.
We're here to see the concert.

Nous sommes là.
We're here.

Vous êtes les bienvenus.
You're welcome here.

Ils sont toujours au coin de la rue.
They're still at the corner of the street.

Tu as été très gentil aujourd'hui, bon chien!
You've been very nice today, good dog!

Il n'a pas été le plus rapide à cette épreuve.
He hasn't been the quickest one at this trial.

Ils ont été les meilleurs.
They've been the best ones.

J'étais en avance cette fois.
I was in advance this time.

Tu étais là avant moi.
You were there before me.

Ils étaient en grève!
They were on strike!

Je serais content d'apprendre qu'elle vient à mon anniversaire.
I'd be happy to learn that she would come to my birthday.

Est-ce qu'elle serait encore en vie?
Would she still be alive?

Si je partais, elle serait déçue.
If I would leave, she would be disappointed.

Je serai millionnaire un jour!
One day, I'll be a millionaire!

Tu seras moins impatient quand
You'll be less impatient when

tu comprendras la chance que tu as maintenant.
you'll understand how lucky you're right now.

On sera toujours en contact.
We'll always be in touch.

Il faut que tu sois compréhensif.
You must be understanding.

Il aimerait qu'on soit plus attentifs.
He'd like us to be more attentive.

Rencontre avec la fleur

Le petit prince traversa le désert et ne rencontra qu' une fleur. Une fleur à trois pétales, une fleur de rien du tout... 
-Bonjour, dit le prince.
-Bonjour, dit la fleur.
-Où sont les hommes ? demanda poliment le petit prince.
La fleur, un jour, avait vu passer une caravane:
-Les hommes ? Il en existe, je crois, six ou sept. Je les ai aperçus il y a des années. Mais on ne sait jamais où les trouver. Le vent les promène. Ils manquent de racines, ça les gêne beaucoup. 
-Adieu, fit petit prince.
-Adieu, dit la fleur.

title: Carnival | Easy Brazilian Portuguese 11
description:
Learn Portuguese with Easy Portuguese: In this episode Silvana shows us carnival in Rio de Janeiro!

GLOSSARY: 

Pra/pro: 
When we want to write the short form, the word "para a / para o" becomes "pra/pro". 

Né: 
We can use “né” to confirm or ask something. 
We can use like “right”, 'see'. 
Carioca: 
Is a Brazilian noun, substantive or adjective used to refer anything related to the city of Rio de Janeiro capital of the homonymous state (Rio de Janeiro), in Brazil. 
Sapucaí: 
The Sambadrome “Marquês de Sapucaí” or simply “Sambadrome” is a purpose-built parade area in downtown Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, where samba schools parade competitively each year during the Rio Carnival. 
The parades attract many thousands of Brazilians and foreign tourists each year. 
Escola de samba: 
Samba school. A samba school is a club or dancing school. 
They practice and often perform in huge square-compounds ("quadras de samba") devoted to practicing and exhibiting samba, an African-Brazilian dance. 
The schools (which are structured more like a guild than a school in the usual sense) have a strong community basis and are traditionally associated with a particular neighborhood. 
Blocos de rua: 
Street Carnival or street parties are street bands that mobilize crowds on the streets and are the main popular expression of Brazilian Carnival. 
Bateria: 
Drums is the percussion band or rhythm section of a Samba School.

title: Differences between the Curitibano and the Paulistano | Easy Brazilian Portuguese 10
description:
Learn Portuguese with Easy Brazilian Portuguese! This time Kristina is out and about in Curitiba to ask people about the difference between Curitibano and Paulistano!

About the episode:

Curitiba has about 1.7m inhabitants and is the capital of the Brazilian state of Paraná. It is considered Brazilians furthest developed big city but still people who come to live in the city complain about the locals being too cold. We went there to find out if that is true or not and found no trouble in finding interview partners. We even need to excuse ourselves for losing the sound material of another six wonderful interviews we had with visitors and artisans. So sorry!

Language details:

Brazilians often use “Ne?” in the end of their sentences in order to confirm what was said before. It is short for “Não é?” (Isn’t it?).

Another very common habit is using examples for what was said in order to make the message clearer. Therefore Brazilians often use “tipo” (just like) in their spoken language.

Informal language example: No Brasil você não precisa pagar uma gorjeta, tipo, quando você vai no restaurante, eles normalmente já incluem 10% do valor da sua conta automaticamente no valor total. (In Brazil you don’t have to pay tips, just like when you go to a restaurant, they usually already include 10% of the value of your bill automatically in the total value.)

Unlike in English, people from a place and their languages are written with small letters.

Example: inglês (Englishman), inglês (the English language)

Draft beer: Is it Chopp or Chope?

Even Brazilians argue about it. In the menu it is usually “chopp” but the pronunciation is “shopi”, which correspondents the Brazilian “chope”. According to the Michaelis dictionary of Brazilian language, chopp is a foreign word that was already integrated in the portuguese language and therefore should also be written in a Portuguese manner, which is “chope”. But since thi version is yet very uncommon, we will continue writing Chopp in our transcriptions.

The verb “tomar” often resembles the English idea of “take” but in contexts with food we sometimes need to translate it as “drink” and sometimes as “eat” and sometimes simply as “have”.

title: Where do you like to travel? | Easy Brazilian Portuguese 9
description:
Learn Portuguese with Easy Brazilian Portuguese: Today Rafael asks people in Marília, Brazil, where they like to travel!

GLOSSARY:

Tá / Tô: 
People often say "você / ele / ela tá" instead of using the complete verb 
"você /ele / ela está". 
Eu estou" becomes "Eu tô". 
Eu estava becomes “Eu tava”. 

Cê/ cês: 
Sometimes, when the speaker wants to say "você/vocês", all that is left of the word is "cê/cês". 

Pra/pro: 
When we want to write the short form, the word "para a / para o" becomes "pra/pro". 

Né: 
We can use “né” to confirm or ask something. 
We can use like “right”, 'see'. 

Ahhan / Ahã: 
We can also use it to confirm a sentence. 
It’s similar to “Uh-huh. 

Assim / Tipo assim: 
We use to express “like this” or “so” 

Nossa: 
Literally means the possessive pronouns “our” but we also use it to express excitement, like “wow”.’

Notes for this episode:

The images look a little old style because we had no other option than filming with a non-HD camera this time. We still hope you enjoy the content of the interviews and wish you a Feliz Natal!
 
DISHES and LANGUAGE:
 
Chester:
This is a chicken with a huge breast part, this the name "chest"+er. It often is cheaper than turkey and therefore very popular.
 
Maionese:
This is a kind of potato salad with a lot of mayonnaise.
 
Galinhada:
This is a mixture of rice and chicken.
 
By the way, you can find some real good Brazilian recipes on this cookery website: http://www.tudogostoso.com.br/
 
 
Amigo Ladrão:
We translated "Amigo Secreto" (secret friend" with Secret Santa, which is the English word for the same game. Amigo ladrão (stealing friend, robbing friend) is a Stealing Santa version, a game also practised in the USA, where the present you got can be stolen in a second round. In the end still everybody leaves with a present, so don't panic.
 
Tá: 
People often say "você / ele / ela tá" instead of using the complete verb "você ele / ela está". Thus "eu estou" becomes "eu tô". 
 
Cê:
Sometimes, when the speaker wants to say "você", all that is left of the word is "cê". But when we want to write the short form the word "você" becomes "vc". The sentence "você está em casa" (you are at home) becomes "vc tá em casa" in a short message.

title: Easy Swedish 1 - Typical Swedish
description:
Learn Swedish with Easy Swedish: Olof is out in Malmö to ask people what's typical Swedish :)

GLOSSARY:

Fika:
Could be a verb: att fika (to fika) or a noun: en fika (a fika). To fika is basically ''to have a coffee'' but often accompanied with pastries. It's often when you take a break from something. Example: you've been out Christmas shopping all day with a friend and then say: ''Vi tar en fika!'' (Let's take a fika). 

Lagom:
Could be a adverb: lagom mycket godis (a suitable amount of candy) or an adjective: temperaturen är lagom (the temperature is moderate). There is no direct translation, but it sort of means: a suitable amout of/moderate/adequate. Many swedes explain it as ''not too much, not too little'', and many think that Swedes are very ''lagom'', not too extreme in any way; that we're moderate.

Jantelagen:
''Jantelagen'' is a bit related to ''lagom''. ''Jantelagen'' says that you're not allowed to succeed too much, you have to stay ''lagom'' (moderate, not too extreme)

These simply omitted the “s” and since there were many of them coming to Brazil between the 1920s and the 1960s, they influenced other native speakers over many generations generations.

Get the show on the road: starting an activity, some kind of work, or a journey

Backseat driver: a passenger sitting anywhere in the car, who tells the driver how to drive; also someone anywhere (not necessarily in a car) who tells someone else how to do something

My way or the highway: you can either do whatever it is the speaker wants to do and however he or she wants to do it, or you can leave 

Hit the road: starting out on a journey or a trip

Put the pedal to the metal: literally means that you should press a car’s accelerator down to the floor; also used when you’re not driving and just means hurry up.

title: #7: Creating subtitles | Easy Languages Tutorials
description:
You want to join the Easy Languages team and produce episodes in your own local language? Check out this tutorial series to see how easy it is to get started.

You are super seriously interested and want to know what's next?
Check out this info:
http://www.easy-languages.org/become-a-co-producer/

And send us an email to info(at)easy-languages.org!

-----
Further info:

Regardless of how you create the subtitle files, you will firstly have to write out the subtitles in a txt document with the original language and then the translation.

Then you have two options:

Option 1 – doing subtitles manually. We have a PSD template that you can open in Photoshop or gimp. Manually edit, then save the files.

Option 2 – Use automation tools to create the subtitles automatically, which requires two steps:

1)      Prepare a txt file whereby subtitles have to be in the following format. If you use a Mac you can even automate this step with software called Ruby.

2)      Open the subtitles template in Photoshop and import the prepared text file to then export the subtitles as individual PSD files. 

If you want to know how that works then you can watch Manuel’s tutorial: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oqO0-k7RP8s

title: Our Project in Namibia with EES | Easy German 86 (Special)
description:
In this special episode of Easy German, recorded at Mauerpark in Berlin, Cari interviews EES about the video project "Never Over" that members of the Easy German crew and The Global Experience realized with Namibian artists EES and Ongoro Nomundu and learners from 5 different schools in Namibia in march 2015.

description: One day while goofing around in the studio with our friend Jason from South Africa, we decided to make a humorous video about Polish swear phrases that foreigners usually wouldn't know. title: Easy Japanese 17 - Onomatope
description:
Mona is out on the streets talking to people about "onomatope". Don't know what that is? Then watch check out this video and the glossary below!

Learn Japanese with Easy Japanese!

-------
Join us on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/EasyJapanese.aritv
-------
GLOSSARY:

*Onomatope: Although in the English language the term onomatopoeia is understood to be limited to words imitating sounds, in the Japanese language "onomatope" includes not only words imitating sounds but also words describing, for example, action, emotion, movement, and shape, which normally don't produce sound.   In the English language, these words are usually called "Ideophone."

*Ono no Imoko: was a Japanese politician and diplomat in the late 6th and early 7th century. 

*giongo: words that mimic actual sounds. 

*gitaigo: words that depict non-auditory senses.

To put something on ice: to postpone something

title: Easy Japanese - Basic Phrases (1)
description:
Learn Japanese with Easy Japanese: In this new video the team of Ari Tv and people in the streets of Sendai help us to learn some basic phrases of Japanese :D

-------
Join us on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/EasyJapanese.aritv
-------
GLOSSARY:

お疲れ様(です)/otsukaresama desu/ It's a very versatile greeting phrase that can have several meanings depending on the situation. The phrase literally means to show appreciation for hard work, and It's most often used in work places. That said, in reality, the usage is very broad. When you come to work in the morning, "otsukaremasa desu" can mean "Good morning" or "Hi"; When you say the phrase at the end of the day, it can mean "See you," "Bye," Thank you." etc.   
In many casual settings, "Otsukaresama desu" is just as saying "how are you?," or"how's it going." 
There is no definite translation as the meaning varies depends on the context.

description:

-------
GLOSSARY:
元気/genki/ adjective: energetic, vigorous,lively, healthy; noun: energy, vigour, health.

お父さん/otousan/ usually means “father,” but here, it’s used as a friendly and respective way to addressing a middle-aged and older man. 

お母さん/okaaan/ usually means “mother,” but here, it’s used as a friendly and respective way to addressing a middle-aged and older woman. 

昔式/based on the old way of calculating age, a new born baby is 1 years old. That is, if you’re going to be 20 years old in December 1st of 2014, you’ve been 20 years old since last year of December 1st.

満/man/ mean “full.” That is, if you are 満 20 years old, you have passed your 20th birthday and your 21st birthday hasn’t arrived yet.

description:
Learn Japanese with Easy Japanese: Today Mona finds out all about Japanese love for Sushi :D

-------
Join us on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/EasyJapanese.aritv
-------
GLOSSARY:

ネタ/Neta/ a specific way to call ingredients on top of sushi rice. It can be seafood, meat, vegetables and whatever you want to put.   

シャリ/Shari/ a specific way to call sushi rice which is rice mixed with vinegar.   

親方/Oyakata/a word for teacher, mentor, or master in certain field. The word literally means “the way of the parent.” Oyakata is more of a father figure.

To lose your touch: to be unable to do something as well as you could before

title: Easy Japanese 6 - Tourism
description:
Learn Japanese with Easy Japanese: Mona visits Matsushima to ask people about tourism in Japan!
-------
Join us on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/EasyJapanese.aritv
-------
GLOSSARY:
Takahagi and Hitachi: citeis in Ibaraki prefecture. 

NTT: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone, a major Japanese Telecommunications company headquartered in Tokyo.

Iwaizumi: It technically is Hiraizumi in Iwate prefecture, which is know for a well preserved group of various temples and gardens, achieved UNESCO World Heritage status in 2011.

Disaster affected areas: Tohoku region was severely affected by the North East Great Earthquake and following devastating tsunami in March 2011. 

Yubatake : literally means “hot water field,” which is often located at Onsen facilities to control the temperature of hot water as well as to produce Yunohona.  Kusatsu Onsen resort has a huge Yubataka right in the center of the resort. 

Yunohana: literally means “flower of hot spring.” It’s also called “sinter,” which is mineral encrustations left by hot springs.

サークル: Circle is a specific way to call student organisations in 
Japanese universities. 
飲み会: Nomikai s a drinking party phenomenon particular to 
Japanese Culture. Nomikai are a part of the culture of most places 
of employment, from schools to nightclubs. They are most often 
held in restaurants or izakaya, usually with everyone seated at one 
large table or occupying a separated section of the venue. 
(Wikipedia). http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomikai
リア充: Riajuu is internet slang for somebody who has a good life. 
It's typically used by otaku and such on message boards like 
2chan to refer to people who have girl/boyfriends and are popular 
with their peers. “Urban Dictionary” 
Today, it is a commonly used slang among young people.

title: Easy Japanese 1 - Typical Japanese
description:
Learn Japanese with Easy Japanese: In our first episode of Easy Japanese Mona takes us around Sendai, asking people what's typical Japanese to them!
***NEW: GLOSSARY***

PRONUNCIATIONS
“wo” becomes “o.”
“wa” is grammatically “ha” , but it pronounces as “wa.”
“iu” usually pronounces as “yu.”

GLOSSARY
Omoiyari: being considerate and thoughtful of the situation and the state of mind of someone other than yourself. The state of having compassion and sympathy toward others.

Omotenashi: Ways in which one welcomes, hosts, and provides service to customers in a heartfelt manner. 

Pretty Cure : http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretty_Cure

Haikyuu!!:  http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haiky%C5%AB!!

Kurobasu: “Kuroko no Basuke” or “Kuroko’s Basketball” http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuroko's_Basketball

Yabai: an expression that indicates possible danger or inconvenience, but it’s also used to describe something that’s great, good, and cool.  

Sasame-yuki: very small snowflakes but bigger than powdery snow. 

Awa-yuki: snow that is soft as if it’s a bubble. It lies on the ground thin and melts away quickly

Wabi-sabi: the virtue of beauty in Japan. It usually indicates simplicity and tranquility. 

Irezumi: tattoo, especially kinds of tattoo worn by Yakuza. 

Otaku: Usually an otaku person has nothing better to do with their life so they pass the time by watching anime, playing video games, surfing the internet - otaku is also used to refer to a nerd/hacker/programmer - “urban dictionary”

title: French Dream Dialogs - Je ne savais pas que vous parliez Français
description:
My French Dream Dialogue is a project in which I imagine talking to somebody in the language I would love to learn to speak: French. While I write down this imaginary dialogue, my friend Anthony translates it and records the voice for me. Now I can learn the dialogue I was dreaming about, and say it in French!

001 
Je ne savais pas que vous parliez Français.
I didn't know that you speak French.
002
Eh bien, c'est parce que je ne parle pas vraiment Français.
Well, that is because I don't really speak French. 
003
Ce serait bien si tous les gens qui ne parlent pas Français parlaient aussi bien que vous.
I wish everybody who didn’t speak French spoke as well as you.
004
En fait, ça fait plus de deux ans que
Actually, I have been trying to learn French
005
j'essaie d'apprendre le français.
for more than 2 years. 
006
Mais je n'étudie pas régulièrement.
But I don't study regularly.
007
Je suis trop paresseux, je m'ennuie trop facilement,
I'm too lazy, too easily bored,
008
et je suis trop pris par d'autres projets.
and too busy with other projects.
009
Alors quel est ton plan pour apprendre le français?
So what is your plan for learning French?
010
sans effort et sans t'ennuyer.
effortlessly and without becoming bored. 
011
Eh bien, j'ai en tête d'imaginer
Well, the plan I have in mind is to imagine
012
que je parle français avec mon ami Anthony.
that I am speaking French with my friend Anthony.
013
Je lui enverrai le dialogue de notre conversation imaginaire et il le traduira pour moi.
I will send him the dialogue of our imaginary conversation and he will translate it for me. 
014
Puis, je l'enregistrerai un jour comme une simple leçon vidéo.
Then one day I will record it as a simple video lesson. 
015
C'est une bonne idée mon ami.
That's a nice plan my friend.
016
J'espère que tu ne finiras pas par te parler à haute voix à toi-même.
I hope you won't end up talking loudly to yourself.
017
Je le fais déjà parfois.
I already do it sometimes.
018
Si tu écris un scénario ou quoi que ce soit incluant des dialogues -
If you write a script or anything that includes dialogues -
019
il devient ensuite plus facile de les apprendre quand on les lit à voix haute.
then you can understand them better when you read them aloud. 
020
Alors, quand est-ce que l'on va voir la vidéo?
So, when are we going to see the video?
021
Tu es déjà en train de la regarder.
You are already watching it.

title: Easy Languages Tutorials -  Choosing your equipment
description:
Wanna become an Easy Languages co-producer? Send your short introduction now to info@easy-languages.org.

You have already been in contact with us and are now ready to become an Easy Languages producer? Great!
Now let's take a look at the equipment.
In this video you'll see Easy Languages producers introducing their equipment to you.

Basically there are two things you need for the production:
a) a camera
b) a microphone

There is a huge range of cameras you can use, starting from good quality smartphone cameras to semi professional or even professional DSLR cameras. Your investment here is between 100€ up to 1000€ or even more.
Important: to produce Easy Languages the camera's built-in microphone is not sufficient. This is because there is often a lot of background noise which is picked up by the built-in microphone and the quality is generally poor. You most definitely need an external microphone. 
For the microphone there is a variety of options: Most Easy Languages producers record with a separate audio recorder like the ones from the ZOOM series, such as those introduced by Ben, Christian and Mato. Another option is a cable connected microphone (however not always convenient when filming on the streets). The most convenient option is the radio microphone (such as the one introduced by Janusz) that automatically synchronises with your video, however this is also the most expensive one. If you do buy a radio microphone then make sure your camera has an external audio input jack - not all cameras provide that option!

Here are the details of the the equipment used by our producers:

Mato and Ana
Video: - Sony CX220 
Audio: Zoom H1

Christian
Video: Canon SX260 HS
Audio: Zoom H1

Ben
Video: Canon 600D
Audio: Zoom H4n

Janusz
Video: Sony HDR - XR 550 
Audio: MIC Sennheiser ew 300 G3
           Receiver: Sennheiser ew 100 G3
