title: Easy English - Doing Verbs
description:
Many English language learners find the present tense very confusing. There are two forms, expressing different functions of the verb. The Simple Present is used for passive statements and repeated actions; i.e. I drink coffee every morning. In the Present Continuous tense, the subject is DOING the verb NOW, in the active present. We hope that you will enjoy our examples in Lennard's Day Off.

title: Easy Thai - Basic Phrases 1
description:
In this video we present you some basic Thai phrases.

"Kha" and "Khrap" are the words that we add at the end of any sentence to make it sound more polite. 
If you are male, you use only the word 'Khrap'.
If you are female, you use only the word 'Kha'.
There are 5 different tones for every single syllable in Thai language. It is somewhat important to keep in mind because if you don't say each syllable in the correct tone, despite pronouncing each word correctly, Thai people might still not understand. 
You don't have to know exactly what those 5 tones are. Just listen to the sentence and pay attention to how high each syllable is compared to each other, and try to imitate roughly (just like singing a song with melodies!). 
In the end, if it's still too complicated, don't worry! Most of the time, thai people can guess what do you want to say.
"Kha" at the end of a question is high while "Kha" at the end of other sentences is low.
"Khrap" is always high.

Subscribe now and receive regular video updates on your favourite languages :)

Ich bin. Die erste Person, singular, vom Verb: sein. 

1
Münster
Münster

Ich bin Münsterarerin.
I am Münsterarerin (from Münster  )

2
gut
good

Ich bin gut. 
I am good.

3
bleiben
to stay

Ich bin so und ich bleibe so!
I am like that and I stay that way.

4
freiwillig
voluntarily

Ich bin freiwillig hier.
I am here voluntarily.

5
verrückt
crazy

Ich bin doch nicht verrückt!
I am not crazy!

5
launisch
moody

Ich bin nicht zickig, nur launisch.
I am not bitchy, just moody.

6
(die) Schuld
blame

Ich bin nicht Schuld!
I am not to blame!

7
wichtig
important

Lasst mich durch! Ich bin wichtig.
Let me through! I am important.


8
(das) Recht
right

Ich bin immer im Recht.
I am always right.

9
(der) Weg
a way

Ich bin auf dem Weg.
I am on the way.

10
toll
great

Ich bin toll. 
I'm great.

11
zu spät
too late

Ich bin zu spät.
I'm late.

12
herrschen
reign

Wo ich bin, herrscht Chaos.
Where I am, there is chaos.

13
einzigartig
unique

Ich bin einzigartig.
I am unique.

14
müde
tired

Ich bin müde.
I'm tired.

15
alt
old

Ich bin nicht alt, ich bin ein Klassiker.
I am not old, I am a classic.

16
immer
always

Ich bin immer für dich da.
I am always there for you.

17
(der) Freund
a friend

Ich bin dein Freund.
I am your friend.
18
(die) Freundin
a friend

Ich bin deine Freundin.
I am your friend.
19
unzufrieden
dissatisfied

Ich bin mit der Gesamtsituation unzufrieden.

20
schlimm - schlimmer - am schlimmsten
bad - worse - worst

Ich bin nicht wie die anderen. Ich bin schlimmer!
I'm not like the others. I'm worse!

21
gewöhnen
accustom

Ich bin daran gewöhnt.
I'm used to it.

Der Infinitiv des Verbs "sein": sein
The infinitive of the verb "to be": to be

1
(die) Frage
qestion

Sein oder nicht sein, das ist hier die Frage.
To be or not to be, that is the question.

2
das muss
it has to

Das muss aber nicht sein.
That need not be the case.

3
das kann
it can

Das kann nicht sein!
It cannot be.

4
es soll
it should

So sollte es sein.
That is how it should be.

5
es darf
it may

Was darf es sein?
What would you like?

6
(die) Stelle
place, position

Ich möchte nicht an seiner Stelle sein.
I do not want to be in his place.

7
(der) Spass
fun

Spass muss sein.
There's no harm in a joke.

8
dass
that

Es kann nicht sein, dass ...
it cannot be, that ...

9
(das) Leben
life

Leben kann auch einfach sein.
Life can also be easy.

10
besser
better

Es könnte nicht besser sein.
It could not be better.

11
ich möchte
I would like

Ich möchte so sein wie er.
I want to be like him.

13
(der) Stolz
pride

Darauf kann er stolz sein.
He can be proud of it. 

14
(der) Ernst
earnestness

Das kann nicht dein Ernst sein!
You can't be serious!

15
immer
always

Du kannst nicht immer 20 sein!
You can not always be 20!

16
unhöflich
rude

ich möchte nicht unhöflich sein.
I do not want to be rude.

17
aber
but

Das mag sein, aber...
That may be true, but...

18
alles
everything

Dabei sein ist alles!
The most important thing is not to win but to take part!

19
froh und munter
happy and cheerful

Lasst uns froh und munter sein.
Let us be happy and cheerful.

20
(die) Angst
fear

Ohne Angst verschieden sein.
Be different without fear.

title: Easy Languages - TGE Youtube Channel Split
description:
We have recently split our Youtube Channel into two!
Why did we do that? Because we do not only want to produce more videos in the near future, but we also want our audience to know what to get on the channel they subscribe to:

EASY LANGUAGES will remain under this url (www.youtube.com/magauchsein) and will offer you about 5 new language videos per week. We are also planning to produce on a more regular level in the languages known already (German, English, Spanish, Arabic) while at the same time explanding the project to new languages such as Dutch, French, Italian, Russian or Croatian. If you enjoy learning languages please subscribe to Easy Languages :D

THE GLOBAL EXPERIENCE's Youtube Channel is from now to be found at www.youtube.com/tge300. This is where you will keep finding all kinds of updates from our global community, like video blogs from the people that go abroad with our organization as well as video reports from our events and projects. Over the next weeks we will slowly move all content not related to language learning from the Easy Languages to the new The Global Experience channel. You will also find annotations with remarks to the new channel location in all videos that are going to be moved soon.

What about magauchsein?
That strange url will remain for now (Easy Languages is still found at www.youtube.com/magauchsein). What is that strange name all about?
That simple: This channel has originally been founded as a channel to broadcast videos from the media workshops we run in schools in Germany. "MAG" is the German abbreviation for  „Medien Arbeitsgemeinschaft" which translates to „media workshop" in English. But since the domain youtube.com/mag has already been taken the day we opened our channel first in 2006, Janusz, our main producer and media trainer, just took the next related suggestion available: magauchsein -- which in german translates to „may be as well". Does not make any sense does it? :)  - Well that time we (and many others) still didnt know what Youtube was, so we left it like that for the beginning. As the number of subscribers grew we were still not moving to a new channel to not loose our subscribers, and thats why we are still with this domain today :)

title: Digital Participation Camp & Summit Review
description:
www.digitalparticipationsummit.org
The Digital Participation Camp & Summit aim at creating an active international network of digital innovators, social entrepreneurs, designers, developers and content creators to unite skills and work together on digital projects for social good. 
The Digital Participation Camp 2013 took place from 19 -- 28 July and brought together 70 young developers, designers, campaigners and activists to live, learn and work together for one week at Schiller High School in Münster, Germany.
The Digital Participation Summit took place on 26 July and invited 120 students and professionals to get to know the DPC projects and meet and discuss with digital innovators from all over the world.

Find out more at www.dpsummit.org

title: Kapenda's Media Internship
description:
Support Kapenda now to achieve his dream and do a media internship in Germany:
www.betterplace.org/en/projects/13504-kapenda-s-media-internship

We have set up this campaign page on www.betterplace.org by The Global Experience and Kapenda in order to make Kapenda's dream come true: a 3-6 month media internship in Germany, starting in November 2013.

AND THIS IS ME, KAPENDA
I am 18 years old and schooling at A.Shipena Secondary School in Namibia. I am hoping to raise 2,500 € for a media internship run by The Global Experience in Germany. Here is my story: I promise that when I am in Germany I will give you regular written and video reports on every project I will be doing and on my whole experience in Germany. It would mean everything to me to start my career in media and I would be very greatful and thank you with my big Namibian heart for every cent that you donate. This is my video for you: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bGxj-9sMIbM

AND THIS IS US, The Global Experience
We are a collective of individuals who work with media to connect young people all over the world. Most of us have been lucky enough to make life changing experiences when staying abroad on another continent. It is these experiences that made us become so passionate about our work today. With our work we aim at giving more young people the chance to make a life changing experience abroad.
Since 5 years we regularly invite students from Asia, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America for intercultural media programs to Germany. 
These workshop and internship programs have not only shaped and changed the life of its participants, but also enriched life and education in Germany. Through our media work we want to make sure that our experiences never just stay among us, but are shared in schools, local communities and even internationally.

OUR PLAN
While being in Germany, Kapenda will not only participate in a multi media training that will be a valuable start for his future career in media and journalism. Through regular photo and video reports Kapenda will also reflect his stay abroad and will help us in Germany to see our society from a different perspective. Through visiting school classes he will furthermore take his intercultural experience into our local schools and help German students to understand more about life in Southern Africa and Namibia in specific.

AND THIS IS WHAT YOU CAN DO
Us, Kapenda and The Global Experience will be greatful for any support you would like to contribute to this project, from large to small. 
This is the first time that we ask our community to support us with the fundraising of such a project due to the lack of public funding opportunities. 
If we succeed with it we can possibly grow even more opportunities like these and have a chance to convince more people and private funders to invest in intercultural education in the future. Thank you so much. We will make sure that every cent that you donate will be worth it.

title: Talking to people in Sheffield (II) | Easy English 3
description:
SUBSCRIBE TO THE NEW EASY ENGLISH CHANNEL: https://bit.ly/EasyEnglishSub
This is part two of Tony in Sheffield. Check out part one here: 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qgiOF3Pa6gE

Glossary:

1 - 'more wilder' is incorrect, it should be 'wilder'.
2 - 'bits and bobs' is a phrase for lots of small things. In this case he is probably meaning that he has been going out to small events here and there, and but not really big nights out.
3 - 'DIY' means Do It Yourself.
4 - 'rough' in this case means 'aggressive'.
5 - 'day bird' would be someone who prefers to do things in the day rather than in the evening or night.
6 - 'wankers' is an offensive term for... hmm... not very nice people! (This comes from the slang verb 'to wank', which is 'to masturbate' - so a wanker would more literally be someone who masturbates, but the insult is not literatal in its usage.)
7 - it is common in English to call someone 'love', regardless of if you even know them, nevermind how much affection of have for them. Although it is more common for females to say when addressing both sexes, and males to say when addressing women, some men with strong Yorkshire (and maybe other, I don't know...) roots will also address other males as 'love'. Just for interest, 'duck' is also commonly heard in Sheffield.
8 - Tony is not addressing just sports fans, and the quiy isn't a sports quiz, but for some reason 'sports fans' has become a phrase - if anyone knows the origin behind this I'd be interested to know!
9 - 'Ta' is a common word for 'thank you'.
10 - 'mate' has become a really common way of informally addressing people, regardless of if the person is a friend or not.
11 - This woman had already ruled out Michael Jackson but was undecided between the other two options. Therefore Tony is saying she had a 50% of getting the answer right when guessing.
12 - 'tough' in this case means 'difficult'.

title: Münster packt's! Der Bürgerpakt für Klimaschutz
description:
Visit our website: http://www.theglobalexperience.org

Ja - ich pack mit an!

Klimaschutz hat in Münster eine lange Tradition und die Stadt ist dafür von der Deutschen Umwelthilfe 1997 und 2006 mit dem Titel "Bundeshauptstadt im Klimaschutz" ausgezeichnet worden. Viele Münsteranerinnen und Münsteraner haben durch ihr Engagement dazu beigetragen, diesen Titel zu erringen. Doch das Thema ist zu wichtig, um sich auf seinen Lorbeeren auszuruhen.

Klimawandel -- das ist kein fernes Zukunftsthema mehr für Experten oder Politiker auf Gipfeltreffen. Er findet bereits statt -- und seine Auswirkungen treffen uns alle.
Die gute Nachricht: Noch ist der Trend zu stoppen, der Schaden zu begrenzen - wir können etwas tun. Deshalb brauchen wir die Unterstützung aller Münsteranerinnen und Münsteraner, denn es sind neben den Anstrengungen auf nationaler und weltweiter Ebene gerade die vielen kleinen Verhaltensänderungen im Alltag, die einen entscheidenden Beitrag zum Klimaschutz liefern.
Die Verwaltungsspitze unterstützt den Bürgerpakt
Die Grundidee des Bürgerpakts sieht folgendermaßen aus: Sie unterzeichnen eine Selbstverpflichtung, um durch einfache Maßnahmen in ihrem persönlichen Alltag dazu beizutragen, das Klima zu schützen. Gleichzeitig bemühen sie sich darum, eine weitere Person aus ihrem Freundeskreis zu gewinnen, ebenfalls etwas zu machen. Die Idee greift um sich und führt zum "Schneeball-Effekt". Wir alle können gemeinsam den Klimawandel aufhalten und unsere Umwelt weiterhin lebenswert zu erhalten.
Sie fragen sich jetzt sicher: "Was soll ich tun und was soll das bringen?" Hier ein Beispiel, das zeigt, dass man mit vielen kleinen Aktionen Großes bewirken kann.
Wenn zuhause Kontrolllämpchen glimmen, weist das auf Stromfresser hin: Ein einziger PC mit einem Flachbildschirm von 17 Zoll braucht im Standby-Modus rund drei Watt pro Stunde. Eine Steckdosenleiste mit Schalter schafft Abhilfe. Damit wird der Computer komplett vom Stromnetz getrennt. Bei rund 100.000 Rechnern in Münsters Privathaushalten werden so allein von 22 bis 6 Uhr 2400 kWh gespart. Aufsummiert auf das ganze Jahr sind das dann 900.000 kWh Strom, die nicht verbraucht werden. Und die Umwelt wird mit über 260 Tonnen CO2 jährlich entlastet.

title: In Memoriam: Taku Mafika
description:
One year ago on this very day we lost our friend and colleague Takunda Mafika at the young age of 27.
Taku was a known musician, passionate teacher and dedicated activist. He was our friend, a good colleague and a role model - not only to his students.
With this video, that contains a collection of outtakes and unpublished video material from his working visits and video shoots in Europe, we want to remember Taku and keep his great spirit alive.
We will not forget you Taku. May your soul rest in Peace. Your spirit will not be forgotten.

To learn more about Taku and his work please visit www.takumafika.com

title: Robson Isaac Shoeslambada - 'Bound to the streets'
description:
Visit our website: http://www.theglobalexperience.org

Zimbabwe Poets for Human Rights
www.facebook.com/zimphr


Bound to the streets
Ragged and funny
In dire need of money
I bruise the pot-holed streets of the city
Maiming the shit-filled alleys and dirty
Daily I play hide and seek with death on the razor-sharp edge of humanity
Once I had a home now I can't pay the dues
Once I went to college now I can't pay the fees
Once I had a wife now I can't pay the price
Poor the result of no economic emancipation
Bound to the street, the result of some people's creation
I a vacuum-filled stomach I try the robbers invention
Maiweeee, I cry in incarceration
This cry my cry that I cry
Bound to the street, Is it god's case?
Bound to the street, the street my place
Bound to the street, the street I hate

Eyes closed,
Tears drop,
The drama of my sleeping mystery
Unfolding before my mental eyes like a tapestry
I ravish and languish in anguish
Feeding on left-overs left by generous shoppers
Hungry I was, am and still will be
The history but of them hitherto societies
Is a history of class struggle and exploitation
How then shall I survive this struggle
In such a society tailor-made to suffer the helpless
Whereby the should-be-helpers are the pioneers of the degradation of human dignity
Benefiting from the suppression, oppression and exploitation of the defenceless
As for me and my street mates
We will travel along
Singing a song
This song, my cry, that I cry
Bound to the street, Is it god's case?
Bound to the street, the street my place
Bound to the street, the street I hate

Yes, you are your mothers daughter
Yes, you are a son to your father
But I have none to call father or mother
You might be coming from far further
You might not be a bird of a feather
But pay no attention to criticism like weather
Rather the bread we gather
Let's break, share and eat together
Until we adopt a new philosophy
I will always cry, this cry my cry 
Bound to the street, Is it god's case?
Bound to the street, the street my place
Bound to the street, the street I hate

title: Chcemy wam pomóc - We want to help you learn the Polish language
description:
Check our blog: http://www.easy-languages.org
Visit our website: http://www.theglobalexperience.org

Chcemy wam pomóc w nauce języka polskiego - We want to help you learn the Polish language

Please support this project. Produce subtitled videos to help people to learn your language!

I would like to invite all of you to a new project. I just uploaded a video where this concept is explained. I would like to produce many subtitled videos to support people learning  your language. The idea is to stand in front of the camera and to tell stories. 

You also learn a foreign language at school. So if you could watch a few subtitled videos with somebody telling your stories from the country  every day and I'm sure that you would learn more and better. 

In my opinion it is also a very good exercise on how to produce media because the task is so clear. You are supposed to stand in front of the camera and tell a story. I hope you will be able to tell a very interesting story. It would be great if your story would be a sort of funny or controversial. Or both. You don't need to learn this story by heart because you are telling it in small pieces, just as we did it in the presentation video.

title: Spiele Melodien nach dem Gehör. Einleitung zum improvisiertem Spiel. (Play tunes by ear)
description:
We are going to present this video in many different languages soon. This one is in German but it's easy to understand what we want to tell you even if you don't speak German.
Our first version was in Polish:
http://youtu.be/EhWmfEE8veU

The video is a simple game actually: we play a simple tune and you are supposed to play it on your own by your ear using all the six positions.  

At the beginning Lisa explains that this tutorial is a continuation of the previous one: How to learn to improvise on guitar in just 5 minutes. Please check it because this tutorial has English subtitles: 

http://youtu.be/4l0nyM4ungg

Then she explains the concept once again: So we're taking only the 7 simple notes: C,D,E,F,G,A,B and we play them in six position so that we can find them easily on the fret-board of your guitar. 

After that it's just a simple game where you won't need any language at all: you listen to a simple melody played in a first position and then you are supposed to pause the video and try to play this melody by ear in all the positions and starting with all "C" notes (because all those melodies start with the "C" note) 

If you can do this then you would probably be able to play any melody you want. 

And this is what we want to achieve. Good luck. 

Please don't forget: to like it, subscribe and click on the advertisement. That would make me very happy :)

title: Interview with Ruprecht Polenz
description:
With its new program "Youth in Dialogue" the german based organization The Global Experience intends to enhance the intercultural dialogue between young people from Europe and Arab and muslim countries. Part of the program is amongst others an international tandem internship program for young people from North Rhine-Westphalia  and Arab and muslim countries, an intercultural workshop program for schools in Germany and two international youth conferences that will be hosted in Münster, Germany in 2012.
In april 2012 we asked Ruprecht Polenz, a german politician who is known for his committment for the euro-arab and christian-muslim dialogue to become the patron of the program "Youth in Dialogue". Ruprecht Polenz is a member of the German Parliament and chairman of the foreign comittee of the german parliament.

On april 18th we met with Ruprecht Polenz at Schillergymnasium Münster and after introducing him to our group and our program we asked him a few questions regarding the international dialogue as well as the intercultural dialogue in Germany.

title: Interview with The Dogg at A. Shipena Secondary School
description:
Yesterday our Namibian-German exchange group had the incredible chance
to not only meet famous Namibian Kwaito artist The Dogg, but also work
with him on his latest music video for the song "Dont' forget".

The video shoot was arranged by Peter and Antra who are currently
working as volunteers of The Global Experience at our partnerschool
A.Shipena Secondary School in Windhoek. Peter also acted as the
director of the video and had worked out the screenplay together with
The Dogg and his management in advance. Then finally, yesterday
afternoon our team started with the realization of the project and

video.

Now it was the turn of the making off team to take an interview with
The Dogg behind the scenes.

title: Students from A.Shipena High School in Windhoek / Namibia invite us to visit them and their county.
description:

This video is one of our first projects: we asked the students to tell us what could we experience in Namibia if we would visit them.

title: How to teach an Englishman to swear in Polish
description:
It's a joke I found on www.kwejk.pl

The joke is that they constuct Polish words using English words. 

Like "Tee who you yeah bunny" stands for "Ty chuju jebany" - which is very a vulgar expression in Polish. 

So I took those sentences and let Ben read them for us. 

The expression are so vulgar that I didn't translate them literary but only in their figurative sense. 

Even if they are very vulgar they will be used very often in Poland but rather only when not seriously meant. 

If ment seriously they can be very insulting so please use them only as a joke between people you really know very well.

title: A Day at A. Shipena school - a video report from our partner school in Namibia
description:
Mr. Adolf Kinde, a teacher of the A. Shipena secondary school in
Windhoek / Namibia has come to visit our school and brought this video
with him.
The history in the video goes like this: First you see some scenes
from the school, students waiting in front of the class and then in
the classroom. Then we see the students at the "soup point", a place
where they have a free meal after the school. Then we see Mr. Adolf
Kinde visiting a parent of one of his student. They live at the
outskirt of the Katutura township called: "Havana". The mother of his
student works only two days in the week. She earns 700 Namibian Dollar
in month (it's about 70 Euro). She has four kids. They money is not
enough to feed them properly.

Das Eine-Welt-Netz Nordrhein-Westfalen besteht in diesem Jahr seit 20

title: Brasilian Students at the Comenius College in Mettingen
description:
The video was produced during the "One World Project Days" at the Comenius College in Mettingen (2011)

We have already the transcription. I will produce the subtitled version as soon as possible.

This is the transcription I got from Rafael Corderio:


1 - Bom, eu gosto muito da escola, na verdade é mais ou menos o que eu tinha esperado né? Eu encontrei pessoas maravilhosas aqui e o curso é também bastante interessante, os professores são muito atenciosos e eu acredito que até o final do ano eu vou viver coisas muito especiais aqui e que vão me ajudar também a estudar aqui na Alemanha

2 - Meu nome é Michele Zamarki (??) eu tenho vinte anos, moro aqui em Mettingen. Estou morando aqui desde fevereiro e eu estou adorando saber que em Mettingen justamente temos um colégio em que representamos o Brasil. No caso é um colégio na Alemanha, especialmente para as pessoas da nacionalidade Brasileira que gostariam de estudar na Alemanha e eu acho isso muito interessante. Estou adorando estar aqui por que eu conheço muitas pessoas da minha cidade, muitas pessoas do meu país, pessoas da minha cultura e mesmo assim a gente está na Alemanha e convivendo com essas pessoas aqui.

3 - Meu nome é Torben Dalibor (??) e eu gosto daqui, é um ambiente novo, inovador eu nao sei. Para mim é diferente. Não tem como comparar o Brasil com a Alemanha, por exemplo. Eu gosto bastante daqui, gosto que tem bastante brasileiro, aí não tenho tanta saudade e... O que que eu faço? Faço o curso M que é para Medicina já que eu quero fazer faculdade de medicina aqui num futuro bem próximo.

4 - Meu nome é Alex e eu sou professor de capoeira. Faço um trabalho há dois anos aqui na Alemanha e todo ano eu estou aqui na escola Medem (??) fazendo este trabalho de capoeira com capoeira Angola, capoeira regional, maculelê. Eu acho assim uma iniciativa muito boa, que incentiva os alunos a um pouco da cultura Brasileira né? Aqui na Alemanha, que aqui não tem muita cultura Brasileira e vem a Capoeira ajudando na parta da Musica, na parte de movimentos, coordenação motora e outros movimentos e é muito legal. Continue assim, todo ano, eu to aqui em Medem (??), realizando esse trabalho de capoeira e é muito legal

title: Miri recites the poem by Rainer Maria Rilke: "Das Karusell"
description:
Inspired by the still existing Merry-Go-Round in the "Jardin du Luxembourg" in Paris, Rilke created one of his most beautiful poems. Reflecting the daily-life expressions of his several stays in Paris, he describes colourful and impressively the roundabaout of roting animals and children and invites the reader into a fantasyworld, where time doesn´t seem to exist ...

Rainer Maria Rilke (1875--1926) is one of most famous poets. With anthologies like "The hour-book", "Sonetts to Orpheus" or the "Duineser Elegies" he created an entire and unique part of German lyrics. Like the popular poem "The Panther" his "Merry-Go-Round" belongs to the "New Poems" of 1907/08.

title: Politics in Mexico according to Diana - Spanish / no subs
description: La política en México pues es bastante complicada. Ahorita está en el poder la derecha, en México, el partido de derecha, y políticas neo-liberales. Hay mucha intervención en nuestra política nacional por parte de Estados Unidos. Durante ya décadas el gobierno ha seguido los intereses de Estados Unidos en detrimento de los intereses nacionales y de la clase trabajadora,  de la gente común y corriente, de los campesinos, etc. Eso lo ha venido haciendo ya desde hace mucho tiempo Y pues bueno, la política en México significa también mucha corrupción. Lamentablemente nuestras autoridades no están conscientes o no les importa sobre las necesidades que tiene el país, las necesidades que tiene la gente y lo único que buscan pues es sacar provecho de sus posiciones y de sus contactos, tratar de obtener ganancias financieras, sacar el mayor dinero que puedan: de los impuestos, de las drogas porque el gobierno está muy coludido con el narcotráfico. El gobierno ahorita tiene una "guerra" contra el narcotráfico, pero esta guerra solo ha significado pues terror, en la sociedad civil; la gente actualmente en México vive aterrada de que en su vecindario ocurra algún enfrentamiento entre el ejército, la policía y los carteles. Es bastante triste. Ahorita hay mucha violencia, la gente está muy enojada, desesperada por la situación porque pues esto no puede seguir por mucho tiempo. Y...¡ah!...pues la política en México....bastante deficiente.

title: Chisomaga 7th report
description:
Check our Solar Net TV Table of Content in order to find more videos you'd like:
http://www.solarnet.tv/forum/index.php?topic=27559.0


Thank God it's Friday, a beautiful autumn day in Münster.

I take my time for a walk through another part of the city; the
waterfront area which has changed in the last few years to a sort of a
bohemian side of the town full of clubs, art studios, and exhibition
space for the local artists.

I decide to visit one of the exhibitions.


(shout out)


I visit the gallery of Ruppe Kosellek. He is a very well known artist
and activist in Germany.

He wants to take over the British Petrolium Company commonly known as BP.

The idea seems crazy to me and so I take my time to talk to him about it.

He tells me that the idea came to him ten years ago while on his
holidays in Holland.

While playing with his daughter on the beach building sand castles he
noticed a strange black substance sticking to her daughter's toes.

After some inspection it turned out to be washed up oil residue.

After this he decided for ecological reasons to collect this oil
residue in plastic bags.

Later he found out that those responsible for this oil residue
pollution was the British Oil Company.

He decided to do something about it.

His plan was simple: he would use the oil residue found on the beach
to make pieces of art, sell them and with the profit he would buy
stock shares of the British Oil Company.

His plan is to become the highest share holder of BP in order to close
it down or to convert it to an environmentally friendly company.

Kosselek travels around the world collecting the oil waste from all
coasts and beaches polluted by BP.

He uses the raw material he brings home to make artworks and paintings.

He sells a wide range of art beginning at a modest two shares
equivalent of BP stock to very expensive paintings.

 He tells me that the real motivation of his actions is to publicize
the ongoing pollution caused by oil companies all over the world.

The recent tragedy caused by the BP oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico
brought a new meaning to his cause. It is not only the ongoing
pollution that is the biggest problem but also the obvious political
power of the Company which frightens Kossele and motivates him to
bring down big oil.

Now Kossele creates a piece of art right before my eyes: his creative
mind converts a normal bank note of one dollar into a dirty "petro"
dollar using the oil residue he scavenges from polluted beaches.

I will buy it for 50 Euro and now I am also contributing to fight oil
companies by using their own coin against them.

Chisomaga is staying with us for the next five weeks. 

We decided to research if the quality of video reports made solely with a small photo camera would be enough for us to watch them without suffering. 

The main problem is not the image, the picture but the sound. We decided to use only the sound recorded by this small camera. 

(in this report we used a canon L11 to record the sound)

The reason to make this experiment is: if we would manage to prove that such reports can reach some minimum of quality then it would show that there are no limits for young people in Africa to produce such reports and share their stories with us. 

Please support our project by giving us your attention; commenting and rating the video. Without your response it wouldn't be half the fun making them.

(Martin speaking)

I was very interested what the other people projects were and so this time I took a microphone with me

title: How to introduce yourself in Germany according to Muriel (no subs)
description:
Check our blog: http://www.easy-languages.org
Visit our website: http://www.theglobalexperience.org
Join our working group: Need German Help?
https://www.facebook.com/groups/434034969992848

I got the transcription and translation from Miki Arimura. Thank you Miki :)

Deutsch:

Hallo, mein Name ist Muriel und ich werde euch heute erzählen, wie man sich in Deutschland vorstellt, beziehungsweise gegenüber anderen Leuten „Hallo" sagt. 
Okay nochmal: (entschuldigung)
Hallo, mein Name ist Muriel und ich werde euch heute sagen wie man sich in verschiedenen Situationen verschieden vorstellt.
Zum einen, wenn man mit Freunden unterwegs ist und du Leute triffst, die du selber noch nicht kennst, sagt man in Deutschland so was wie „Hi, wie geht's" oder „Mein Name ist Muriel und gehe auf die und die Schule". Man Siezt die Leute nicht sondern Duzt sie nur und fängt meistens mit ihnen einen Smalltalk an und erzählt ihnen halt was man heute noch macht beziehungsweise was man die Tage noch machen wird. So was wie „Was machst du heute noch?" „Sieht man sich mal auf der und der Party?" oder ähnliches.
Zum anderen stellt man sich ganz anders vor, wenn man mit erwachsenen Leuten redet zum Beispiel, wenn man sich in einem Beruf vorstellt geht man hin und begrüßt Leute mit „Schönen guten Tag. Ich bin sehr froh, dass ich von ihnen angerufen wurde" ... und drückt die eigene Freude aus, dass man sich vorstellen darf und für den Beruf vorgeschlagen wurde. Dann erzählt man etwas von seinem Leben und verabschiedet sich nachher mit „Vielen Dank, dass ich mich hier vorstellen durfte. Ich hoffe man sieht sich in der Zukunft."
Dann gibt's noch andere Gründe zum Beispiel wenn man sich im Ausland vorstellt, dann sagt man ebenfalls erst den Namen meistens nicht den vollständigen man sagt woher man kommt zum Beispiel „Mein Name ist Muriel, ich komme aus Deutschland." Und man sagt was man hier in diesem Land vorhat und warum man hier ist zum Beispiel „Ich komme hierher da ich mit der Schule hier bin und ich möchte gerne den Eiffelturm sehen." Und verabschiedet sich nachher mit „Es hat mich gefreut Sie kennen zu lernen."
Danke, das war's.









English:

Hello, my name is Muriel and today I'm going to show you how to introduce yourself in Germany or rather how to say "Hello" to other people.
Okay once again ... (Sorry)
First, when you're in Germany with your friends and you meet people you don't know, you say things like "Hi, how are you?" ( "Hi, wie geht's?" ) or "My name is Muriel and I'm going to the ...(name of the school)." ( "Mein Name ist Muriel und ich gehe auf die ...(Name der Schule/name of the school). Schule.". You don't use „Sie" (= you -- polite form) but you use "Du" (= you impolite form). And mostly you start a to talk a little about what you're going to do the today or rather the next few days. Then you say something like that "Was machst du heute noch?" = "What are you going to do today?" or "Sieht man sich mal auf der und der Party (von diesen Leuten/from those people)" = "Hope we'll meet at "this or that" ( = name of the Person's party) Party!" or something like this.
Secondly, you introduce yourself on a completely different way, if you're talking to adults for example when you introduce yourself for a job. Instead of "Hallo/Hi/..." you say "Schönen guten Tag" = "nice day" (if you say this, you wish those people a nice day -- but you use it as "hello" and it's also polite!) Then you probably should say "Ich bin sehr froh, dass sie mich angerufen haben!" = "I'm very happy, that you called me." (for that job..) and you should show, that you're really happy, that you're allowed to introduce yourself for that job or rather that you got suggested for this job. Then you tell them something about your life and finally you say "Vielen Dank, dass ich mich hier vorstellen durfte. Ich hoffe, man sieht sich in der Zukunft." = " Thank you very much, for letting me introduce myself for that job. I hope we'll see each other/ meet in the future." (probably meant that you hope you'll get the job).
Then there's another reason for introducing yourself on a different way for example in a foreign country. Then you also tell them your name, but mostly only your first name. You also say from where you are. For example : "Hallo mein Name ist Muriel, und ich komme aus Deutschland. " = "Hello my name is Muriel and I'm from Germany." You also say, what you're going to do in that country and why you're there (here) for example : "Ich komme hierher, da ich mit der Schule hier bin und ich möchte gerne den Eiffelturm sehen." = "I'm here with my school class and I wish to see the Eiffel Tower.". At last you say "Es hat mich gefreut sie kennen zu lernen." = „I'm happy that I've met you/ It was nice to meet you/... ." 
Thanks, that's it.

Chisomaga is staying with us for the next five weeks. 

We decided to research if the quality of video reports made solely with a small photo camera would be enough for us to watch them without suffering. 

The main problem is not the image, the picture but the sound. We decided to use only the sound recorded by this small camera. 

(in this report we used a canon L11 to record the sound)

The reason to make this experiment is: if we would manage to prove that such reports can reach some minimum of quality then it would show that there are no limits for young people in Africa to produce such reports and share their stories with us. 

Chiso uses the Magix video editing program. 

Please support our project by giving us your attention; commenting and rating the video. Without your response it wouldn't be half the fun making them.

hey I'm Chisomaga , this is my fourth report
today I'm in the middle of Münster

I'm working with Sandra and Janusz
Sandra is taking the notes and Janusz will do the video taping
so I can concentrate on my presentation.
Today there is a cultural festival dedicated to the foreigners living in Münster.
During this festival they have the opportunity to present their different cultures.
There are many stand where they display cultural artifacts, cuisines and info material about  their projects.
I meet Mr Spyros Marinos who is the president of the integration council in Münster.
He is telling me that the foreigners in this city participate in the political activities of the municipality.
The mayor of Münster Markus Lewe gave the opening speech.
After this I wanted to ask him a few questions,
but he scheduled to meet me in his office the next day.
So prepare for my next report where I will make an exclusive interview with him.
Now I go to see what is happening around.
I met people from Nigeria. I talked to Susane Ndawike. She lives in Münster for a long time.
She is with her fellow Nigerian women here, and they are going to perform a cultural dance from Ibunam.
I know those dances well because I also come from the same state as them.
The music and the dances make me feel at home in Münster.
Later I met other Nigerians , they are from a faith based organization (FBO)
Their agenda is to bring people to God.
They organize church services to people from Africa.
Also our people from Solarnet use the opportunity to present our projects
where we are explaing our projects of the making video language with foreigners living in Münster.
One of the persons who visited our stand was the bishop of Münster Friedrich Ostermann.
I told him about my project. He was very interested, especially because he helped us financially
to organize our seminar.
I was very surprised he knew a lot about Nigeria.
This is because his church runs many projects in my country.
We meet two girls filming for a project for the academy of arts in Münster.
They have a very nice camera with the external mic connection.
Something that is quite seldom nowadays, most of the small cameras don't have them.
This draws our attention and we engaged in a discussion with them.
At the end Jansz gets Interviewed by them: they asked him if he was happy
and Janusz, you know him, is happy to answer.
Then I met Barbara Kemmler,  she leads a theater group called "Cactus Young Theater".
She likes to work with kids of immigrant parents.
The performance you see is part of a project, she invited us to the premiere of her new theater drama.
At the end i met George Sakaladis.  He comes from Greece.
He studied in Münster and he is now working in a cultural integrational council.
He told me that the theme: "cultural integration" is very important at the moment in Germany.
The city runs a lot of projects to make the foreigners to feel at home in Münster
but also to feel responsible for the development of the society they are living in.

WOW it was a nice activity for me, as you can see today was the BOMB
watch out for my reports , (one love)

title: Chisomaga's First Report
description:
Check our Solar Net TV Table of Content in order to find more videos you'd like:
http://www.solarnet.tv/forum/index.php?topic=27559.0

Watch all Chisomaga's reports on Solar Net TV Table of Content:
http://www.solarnet.tv/forum/index.php?topic=30729.0

Chisomaga is staying with us for the next five weeks. 

We decided to research if the quality of video reports made solely with a small photo camera would be enough for us to watch them without suffering. 

The main problem is not the image, the picture but the sound. We decided to use only the sound recorded by this small camera. 

The reason to make this experiment is: if we would manage to prove that such reports can reach some minimum of quality then it would show that there are no limits for young people in Africa to produce such reports and share their stories with us. 

Chiso uses the Magix video editing program. 

Please support our project by giving us your attention; commenting and rating the video. Without your response it wouldn't be half the fun making them.

title: How to greet people in England according to Ben.
description:
Check our Solar Net TV Table of Content in order to find more videos you'd like:
http://www.solarnet.tv/forum/index.php?topic=27559.0

Hello, my name is Ben and I'm from York in England, and today I will talk to you about how we greet each other in England.
So firstly, I will say about the formal meetings. So if you want to be really formal you can meet the Queen. I have never done this, but it is common courtesy to bow when you meet the Queen. So you just move forward like this and take her hand like "Hello Madame", like that.
 And then with obviously a less important person, for example a family member maybe, or someone in a job interview, it is always a handshake. So just like that, maybe three or four pumps on the shake. And then... erm... orrr... erm. So often people like to kiss each other on the cheek. But yeh, that's more like a family member, a kiss on the cheek. Maybe two but most likely one. 
And then in an informal situation, maybe to do with the hands you might maybe tap like this, but that's a bit more American, maybe a bit gangster. But often, sometimes with my friends I do a handshake and then click. But in terms of words, we often say "mate" at the end of things which is quite funny because we always - mate means friend - we always say it to people who we have never met before, so it's quite a strange thing. "Alright mate?" or "Hello mate, how you doing mate?". 
I know that other cultures find this one quite funny. But then there are lots of different words for mate. There's bud, or hmm... pal is another good one, however mate is the most common. We usually say hi or hey, or alright. Now one awkward situation I frequently find myself in is when, for example, I say "Alright?" when I walk past somebody. However some people think I am saying "Are you alright?" and so they say "Yeh I'm OK thanks, are you?" and I'm thinking "Oh, err I have to respond!". 
"OK, erm yes I'm OK. Err yeh great, bye!" But I don't really want to speak to them, I just want to say "Alright", as in, you know, "Hello". Hello, yeh... And obviously "Hello" is the most common one which you will learn as a foreign speaker. Oooh, I'm trying to think of more things to say... Erm I would say that's probably it. And that is how you most likely greet each other in England. Thank you.

title: Easy German Basic Phrases - Hospitality
description:
We did this video during our visit by our partner school in Baumgartsbrunn / Namibia. This year we invited 4 students of Robert-Wetzlar-Berufaskolleg from Bonn. Those students worked on various projects with the girl of the Domestic Institute. One of the project was to make a list typical sentences the Namibian students could need when working in any touristic facility and addressing a German tourist. 

This video is a result of this project.

Easy Languages is a non-profit video project aiming at supporting people worldwide to learn languages through authentic street interviews. We also use this format to expose our street culture  abroad and create a more diverse image of our countries. Episodes are produced in local languages and contain subtitles in both the original language as well as in English.

More information at 
http://www.easy-languages.org/
http://www.facebook.com/easylanguagestreetinterviews

Easy Languages is produced by the intercultural youth media network The Global Experience:
http://www.theglobalexperience.org
http://www.facebook.com/theglobalexperience

title: Videofilm im Internet als neue Chance der interkulturellen Kommunikation
description:
Dieser Film ist entstanden am Comenius Kolleg im Rahmen der "Eine Welt Tage" vom 8.9. bis 10.9.2009

Produziert von: 
Chandrima Philipp
Bastian Leeker
Simon Plumpe


Today is the 8th September 2009. We are at the Comenius School in Mettingen. This week our school hosts the so called ‚One World Days in which many different workshops and projects take place. Our group works on the topic intercultural communication in the Internet. 

There are many ways and opportunities to communicate with people from all over the world. Nowadays the most frequently used way of communication is the Internet. Emails, chat rooms, instant messenger services and forums are only some of the Internet services we use everyday to keep in contact with each other.

One medium is especially useful : The video in the Internet. We use videochats, watch the news on the Internet and laugh about funny videoclips on YouTube. Producing and publishing movies  it seems like everybody can do this  but does everybody really do it?

The question is : Why would I want to make or watch a movie?

Videos in the Internet  is that only an alternative to TV? No  the strength of the Internet lies somewhere else  because here we are able to see things that are not avaliable on TV! We can learn about the everyday life of people in other countries, we can create an awareness of their problems, that no-one notices, can communicate with our friends and partners from all over the world and learn from one another (free from stereotypes and free from the one-sided perspective that is shown on TV).

And the most important is : Everyone can do it! For the last ten years computers, cameras and software were for most people too expensive  Today anyone can make videos! Even in the poorer regions of the world, we find people with digitalcameras and basic computers  all you need in order to produce a small video.

Today we would like to show you, how easy it is for someone to make a film! In our example we produce a shortfilm, in order to establish a communication between our school in Germany and our partner school in Brazil.

The most important aspect in this project is the text, this is because it contains all the information and motivates the listener to listen to the film.

Scene 1
The student chooses a theme and then writes a text  for example he introduces himself. Here he discusses his first draft of the text with his teacher.
The text is then recorded  this is the most difficult part, even though you can achieve a good result with a basic headset.

Then you collect the footage. You can do this with a basic digital photo camera with a videofunction  this quality is even more than it is required for the Internet!


Audio and video are then cut and put together with a simple program until you have a short film you can send via email or publish on your own homepage.

Imagine all schools would use this easy way to communicate with their partnerschools. We could learn from each other a lot and keep in contact  even over great distances between continents and oceans. Because communication is the best way to fight against prejudices and racism. Only when we know and understand each other we can make a change!



My name is Ramon. I study here because I want to go to university in Germany. I hope we could show you how easy it is to produce a film.

title: On the same road
description:
This video has been produced during the 3rd international Solar Net Youth Seminar in Germany and Poland 2009 in order to promote the World March of Peace and Nonviolence 2009.

Spoken text:

[Portuguese]

One...
Two....
Three...

Did you know that every three seconds a person starves to death in the world?

[Vietnamese]
Meanwhile nations are spending billions just to increase their arsenals.

[Polish]
The fact is that we're all on the same road, but are we heading in the right direction?

[Spanish]
This road that should pull us all together, also has the power to lead us astray.

[Ukrainian]
On this road there should be no one going faster or slower. 

[Dutch]
There is no place for hate and hunger in a world of tolerance, justice and equality.

[Turkish]
This is the road of life, which must be enjoyed at every single moment.

[Oshiwambo]
It has in it complexities and mysteries, and should unite whole nations in common issues.

[Arabic]
The same power that put us in a war against each other, where at the end there are no winners or heroes.

[Malay]
Just people that forgot the real meaning of the road... to live with respect and dignity. 

[German]
We are all travellers on this endless road, and it's up to us to make sense of our journey.

[Russian]
So let's open our hearts during this journey, let's share together the joy and bliss that this road can provide.

Come on, join us!

title: gebet ist gut - fair trade ist besser
description:
From 2. till 9 April 2009  the 4th International Media Workshop organized by the Franz Hitze Haus took part in Münster in cooperation with the Dethloff German School in Lublin / Poland.

There were over 20 participants from Poland and 10 from Germany.

The general theme of the meeting was: Creative Advertising. We decided to produce advertising attempts to the them "Fair Trade". 

There were 4 groups: theater, radio, print and video group.
The video group consisted of 8 people, three students from Germany and 5 from Poland.

We split our group in three teams.

We thought over our task and decided to produce three videos: two advertising clips and one video report to the theme.

This is one of our video clips: prayer is good - fair trade is better.

title: everyone calls me Henny
description:
Join our working group on Facebook: Need German Help?
Check our blog: www.easy-languages.org
Visit our website: http://www.theglobalexperience.org

This is a video made under the "easy made" concept terms by Henriette.

"Easy Made" means: All video footage was made by a normal standard (photo) camera, with it's "video" function. We used the Panasonic DMC - TZ3 LUMIX.

It also means, that the editorial concept is very simple. Henny has written the text for her video in a few minutes.

Technically speaking the video is mainly the text written and read aloud by Henny on which we put some video footage. 

Our aim is to encourage other people to produce videos under the similar "easy made" concept.

title: Wolfgang Zropf
description:
We made the video during an ENSA Seminar in Katlenburg (Germany). 

We made a lecture on how easy it is to make a video and introduced our concept of simple made videos. 

Mr. Wolfgang Zropf participated in the schooling and he has written the text. We managed to record his voice and to gather some simple video footage of him.

The film should be an example of how easy it is to produce such simple videos. 

The main features are: the video footage is taken with an simple photo camera (Panasonic DMC - TZ3 LUMIX), the audio of the raw video is deleted, the video consist of a quickly, spontaneously written text, recorded and edited with Audacity (free) and few also very quickly made video takes. 

Conclusion: It is so simple that everybody can do it. So please join us :)

http://www.theglobalexperience.org

title: Polish Lessons -- Unit 24
description:
My plan is to produce one short video for every letter and every sound of the Polish Language.

At the end there will be approximately 45 videos, every one of them containing 17 words.

So theoretically somebody, who would spend 45 minutes watching all of them, would have at least a swift contact with 765 Polish words (mainly substantives)

There is a myth that the Polish Language is one of the most difficult to learn. I don't believe it anymore after meeting and speaking to a lot of students who after learning Polish for six months or so - mastered this language to a remarkable degree.

My theory is that the Polish Language appears very difficult at the beginning but after somebody manages to reach a certain point of knowledge - this language becomes unexpectedly easy to speak - because obviously it is a very intuitive and "judge by the ear" language.

After reaching a certain point you just know how to say it (how to decline and so) because it seems to sound either good or not.

So this is why I think, that anybody who would like to learn Polish should invest quite an ample time to "get used" to it.

Those 45 minutes of the Polish alphabet are supposed to be the first introduction to this foreign language. It should help to understand how Polish should be pronounced as well as to learn some first Polish words.

It should give you the general idea of how the Polish language sounds like.

In the next level we will deal with most common verbs. We will look at how they sound and function.

I dedicate this course to Carina and Manuel who are trying to learn Polish. I hope I can help you. You can imagine how happy I would be to speak Polish with you.

title: Polish Lessons -- Unit 16
description:
My plan is to produce one short video for every letter and every sound of the Polish Language.

At the end there will be approximately 45 videos, every one of them containing 17 words.

So theoretically somebody, who would spend 45 minutes watching all of them, would have at least a swift contact with 765 Polish words (mainly substantives)

There is a myth that the Polish Language is one of the most difficult to learn. I don't believe it anymore after meeting and speaking to a lot of students who after learning Polish for six months or so - mastered this language to a remarkable degree.

My theory is that the Polish Language appears very difficult at the beginning but after somebody manages to reach a certain point of knowledge - this language becomes unexpectedly easy to speak - because obviously it is a very intuitive and "judge by the ear" language.

After reaching a certain point you just know how to say it (how to decline and so) because it seems to sound either good or not.

So this is why I think, that anybody who would like to learn Polish should invest quite an ample time to "get used" to it.

Those 45 minutes of the Polish alphabet are supposed to be the first introduction to this foreign language. It should help to understand how Polish should be pronounced as well as to learn some first Polish words.

It should give you the general idea of how the Polish language sounds like.

In the next level we will deal with most common verbs. We will look at how they sound and function.

I dedicate this course to Carina and Manuel who are trying to learn Polish. I hope I can help you. You can imagine how happy I would be to speak Polish with you.

title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
description: Who is the great dragon whom the spirit will no longer call lord and god? "Thou shalt" is the name of the great dragon. But the spirit of the lion says, "I will." "Thou shalt" lies in his way, sparkling like gold, an animal covered with scales; and on every scale shines a golden "thou shalt." Values, thousands of years old, shine on these scales; and thus speaks the mightiest of all the dragons: "All value of all things shines on me. All value has long been created, and I am all created value. Verily, there shall be no more 'I will.'" Thus speaks the dragon.

title: Lecciones automáticas del español - El segundo intento (2)
description:
This is a very simple idea. I want to try to learn Spanish all by myself using the "text to speech" (AT&T Labs Demo) and "google.com/translate" Programs.


I would be very grateful if some Spanish native speaker would correct any mistakes which accrue in the text. Then I would have a chance to improve it.


I have no idea if those lessons can be of any use to anybody else but they are very good to me, because playing around with this concept I force myself playfully to learn Spanish.

I did it very quick (50 words in 81 sec) so that it wouldn't be that boring to repeat watching the video. If you want to slow it down - use the pause button.

- At this I uploaded my (self made) lesson and just a day after Trapper0707 has commented:

Hi. I´m Spanish. (my English isn´t very good but I´ll try to explain...) I´m sorry but I´ve found a lot of mistakes. Spanish is talked in very different ways depending in which country you are. I think the translator uses Spanish from some South America country because there are a lot of words which are a bit or completely different from the ones used in Spain. For example i´ll write some wrong words and the correct translation:
(...)
Oh, and if you want and advise, to make you video popular write better tags (in English) like : Spanish, learn, words, ...

good luck with your learning!

And he acctually corrected 12 words! 

So I answered:
This is so great, Trapper - thank you so much. I was hoping that somebody would help me and would correct my mistakes. But still it is such a nice feeling that it happened so straight away.

I will correct now my lesson and I will replace the film. I hope you will be so nice and continue to correct my further attempts. 
Please look up the video we made to introduce our project, it is in my account just in the front: Solar Net International - Introducing to the project, maybe you could imagine to stay in touch with us.

So the video you see now is the corrected one. 

And the next video I'm going to do will be without the Spanish words at first at I hope Trapper0707 will write them down for me :)

title: KhoeKhoegowab Lesson No:4
description:
KhoeKhoegowab is the most populous and widespread of the Khoisan languages. It belongs to the Khoe language family, and is spoken in Namibia, Botswana, and South Africa by the Namaqua, Damara, and Haillom, as well as smaller ethnic groups such as the #Khomani. The name for Nama speakers, Khoekhoen, is from the Nama word khoe "person", with reduplication and the suffix -n to indicate the plural.

Thusnelda Dausas and Gabriel /Khoeseb are two young teachers from the primery school, a small school vilage called Baumgartsbrunn in Namibia.

title: /Nama ma te by Raphael and Pele perf. by Gabes
description:
Thusnelda Dausas and Gabriel Khoeseb are both young teachers from our partner school in Baumgartsbrunn/Namibia. They spend two weeks in December 2006 visiting our school, Schillergymnasium/Münster in Germany. Most of their time they spend in the media workshop working with us on our internet communication project. 
The footage was taken by little LUMIX photo camera. I didn't even know by then I was going to use it for the clip so the situations are quite random.
Gabes is a great fun of the Namibian Musicians Raphael and Pele. He introduced us to their music in a special radio program we produced together. The song he is singig comes from a CD by Pele and Raphael: Xai//na #Gomasen, the song title is: /Namma ma te.
Raphael and Pele's record label is the WMP (Welwitschia Music Production base in Swakopmund, Mondesa (Namibia). 
Please visit their Website: www.welwitschiamusicproduction.wideweb.co.za
I hope they don't mind us taking their song for our little remembrance clip.

title: Die Erneuerbaren Energien in Ghana - Part 3
description: Die Jatropha ist eine von über 200 Pflanzen auf unserem Planeten, aus denen Öl gewonnen werden kann, das als alternativer Kraftstoff, z.B. als Dieselersatz, verwendet werden kann. Im Norden Ghanas hat die ghanaische Umwelt- schutzorganisation RENERG gemeinsam mit Partnern aus Deutschland ein Pilotprojekt gestartet, dessen Erfolg nicht nur dem Umweltschutz zu Gute käme, sondern auch der Bevölkerung im Norden Ghanas. Zwei Wochen lang begleiteten wir die ghanaische Umweltschutzorganisation bei ihrer Arbeit mit Erneuerbaren Energien in Ghana. Dieser Film zeigt Möglichkeiten, Probleme und Chancen der Arbeit mit regenerativen Energien in dem westafrikanischen Land. Eine Produktion von Solar Net International e.V. Kamera & Schnitt: Carina Schmid Sprecher: Harald Redmer Tontechnik: Georg Türk Format: DVD Pal Laufzeit: ca. 20 Min. © Münster 2006

title: Good Coffee Exercise - Roestbar
description:
The concept of our Media Workshop Groups (one in Germany/Münster the other in Poland/Katowice) include the idea of task of the month. 
Every month the participators of the Media Groups are supposed to work on an exercise witch has the same medium and theme.   
We've got 10 exercises in an school year. Two of them concern creative writing, four are about making pictures and graphics, four about making films.
The hope is, that when the two groups will work on the same themes there will occur common fields of interest, common experiences to exchange, joint action in some cases and so on. With one word: we work together and we inspire each other to work.  
One of the task of the month exercises last year was to improvise a film on a theme: good coffee. 
It should be also done with the very basic equipment. We wanted to convince everybody that you don't need an expensive gear to start making films. 
This film exercise was made by Max and Maris.

title: Gypsy Dance
description:
This video is already pretty old. The comments it gets are very similar. So this is why I have deactivated the comment function. 

Music: "Nane Tsoha" and "Loli Phabay"

In July 2006 we hold the first german-polish youth-media seminar, organized in cooperation of Solar Net International and Palace of Youth in Katowice. Our group was part of the 7th International Meeting of Youth "Europe of Peace".
We met there a group of girls from Slovakia who participated in the event. They organized a slovakian-polish Dance Workshop. The girls are students of Renata Madaraszova school of arts from Senec near Bratislava.
We have spontaneously decided to make a videoclip of the dancing girls. They do a gypsy dance.  
We did it with one cheap photo camera and edited it very quickly by synchronizing 4 or 5 tracks and then just choosing sequences we wanted to keep.
Next year they want to establish kind of applied internet media subject in their school so I hope we are going to see and hear more from them
